latest.title: Is global positioning better for pharmaceutical advertising? An experimental study on its impact on brand equity
latest.venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose To enhance efficiency in pharmaceutical advertising, this study aims to examine and compare the effects of consumer culture positioning (CCP) – global (GCCP) versus local (LCCP) – and doctor recommendations in direct-to-consumer advertising (DTCA) on skepticism, attitude toward the ad (Aad) and customer-based brand equity (CBBE) and examine the mechanisms through skepticism and Aad. Design/methodology/approach A 2 (CCP: GCCP vs LCCP) × 2 (doctor recommendation: with vs without) between-subject factorial experiment was conducted. Hypotheses were tested using the General Linear Model (GLM) and PROCESS Model 4. Findings CCP significantly influences skepticism, Aad and CBBE, whereas doctor recommendations do not. GCCP generates higher Aad and CBBE and lower skepticism than LCCP. Skepticism and Aad also significantly mediate the effect of CCP and doctor recommendations on CBBE. Research limitations/implications Future research could examine how artificial intelligence and social media influence the effectiveness of GCCP in DTCA, assess GCCP effectiveness across countries and cultures, explore the interpersonal dynamics of doctor recommendations and investigate gender differences in skepticism toward DTCA using GCCP. Practical implications Pharmaceutical companies may consider GCCP in DTCA to improve advertising efficiency through standardized global advertising while enhancing CBBE. Its greater effectiveness than doctor recommendations also suggests more efficient allocation of promotional expenditure. Originality/value This study extends the DTCA literature by examining consumer culture positioning as a previously overlooked determinant of DTCA effectiveness. The findings of this study demonstrate that GCCP can enhance CBBE by reducing skepticism and increasing Aad.

latest.title: Price Competition Under Platform-Mediated Search: A Consider-Then-Choose Framework
latest.abstract: Problem definition: We study the problem of predicting price equilibria on e-commerce platforms where sellers compete across multiple attributes (e.g., price, average rating, delivery speed). In these settings, a platform’s design choices — such as its display ranking, filtering tools, and promotional badges — critically shape customer search and purchase behavior, which in turn determine sellers’ equilibrium pricing strategies. Our goal is to develop a tractable framework that allows a platform to anticipate the market impact of its design interventions. Methodology/results: We consider a behavioral model — Consider-then-Choose with Lexicographic Choice (CLC) — specifically tailored to platform-mediated search. We establish that any local Nash equilibrium admits a sequential-move characterization; this yields a tractable procedure for computation under an interpretable sufficient condition, which we term gradient dominance. We further prove that under gradient dominance, simple, decentralized gradient-based algorithms converge to an equilibrium, providing platforms with a method for simulating market outcomes. Finally, we use our framework to study how platform design affects market outcomes. Managerial implications: Our framework applies to any platform in which sellers compete on multiple attributes and customer choice is guided by the platform’s interface. In these environments, sellers’ pricing strategies must be understood not in isolation, but as a response to the platform’s design. Our work provides platform operators with a rigorous toolbox to efficiently evaluate how changes to interface design, information disclosure, and ranking policies can affect competitive outcomes.

latest.title: ProactiMate: evaluating LLM-based chatbots for behavior change interventions
latest.abstract: This paper explores the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in promoting sustainable behavior, specifically in overcoming procrastination. Despite widespread recognition of the need for sustainable behavior change, individuals often struggle to break free from entrenched, unsustainable habits. LLMs, such as OpenAI’s GPT-4, represent a significant breakthrough in artificial intelligence and are increasingly used in behavior change interventions. This study introduces ProactiMate, a chatbot built using Motivational Interviewing (MI) principles and a Chain of Models approach for prompt engineering, designed to help users combat procrastination. Our research compares four LLMs (GPT-3.5 Turbo, LLaMA-3.2, Qwen-2.5, and SmolLM-1.7B) for output influence on procrastination avoidance, and assesses the impact of hyperparameters (temperature and top-p values) on procrastination avoidance. The findings reveal that GPT-3.5 outperforms other models across various evaluation metrics, and higher temperature and top-p values lead to more effective procrastination avoidance from automatic evaluation. According to expert evaluations, Qwen-2.5 and GPT-3.5 Turbo demonstrated notable effectiveness in fostering user engagement and motivation for addressing procrastination, with GPT-3.5 Turbo particularly distinguished by its capacity to provide strategies that help maintain long-term motivation. And GPT’s output aligns well with both automatic evaluation metrics and human evaluation. The results provide insights into the most effective ways to use LLMs in chatbot design, offering solutions for future usability testing.

latest.title: Optimal free energy requirements for managing disruptive and unexpected organizational change
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a systems-theoretic framework to understand how organizations maintain adaptive functioning amid disruptive, unexpected environmental change. Drawing on the free energy (FE) principle, the paper conceptualizes organizational FE as an adaptive reserve capacity that enables organizations to absorb, interpret and respond to environmental uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach Using archival data from Canadian manufacturing sectors during the COVID-19 disruption period, the study explores whether pre-pandemic levels of FE, operationalized through manufacturing capacity utilization, were associated with post-pandemic organizational resilience and GDP growth between 2019 and 2023. The analyses also examine the potential roles of automation, government stimulus and supply-chain disruption within a moderated mediation framework. Findings The analysis provides no evidence that FE directly predicts post-pandemic GDP growth. However, FE consistently predicts sector-level organizational resilience measured through absorptive, adaptive and recovery capacities. These findings suggest that adaptive reserve capacity may operate more meaningfully at organizational and sectoral levels than as a direct driver of macroeconomic performance. Practical implications The study contributes to resilience and systems research by reframing FE as a resilience-oriented systems construct associated with adaptive capacity amid uncertainty. The findings further suggest that systems optimized exclusively for short-term efficiency may become more vulnerable to brittleness during large-scale disruption. Originality/value This paper integrates systems theory, organizational resilience research and adaptive systems perspectives into a novel interdisciplinary framework for

latest.title: A bibliometric and content analysis of marketing in Web 3.0
latest.abstract: The transition to Web 3.0 driven by blockchain, non-fungible tokens (NFTs), and the metaverse presents a transformative paradigm shift for digital marketing. Yet, the current body of academic research remains notably fragmented. This study systematically maps the intellectual structure of Web 3.0 marketing to consolidate existing knowledge, uncover dominant trends, and propose a cohesive agenda for future research. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a comprehensive bibliometric and content analysis of 121 documents from the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection spanning 2009 to 2025. Leveraging analytical tools including Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CitNetExplorer, the study maps citation networks, keyword co-occurrences, and bibliographic coupling. The findings demonstrate an exponential surge in academic interest starting in 2021 and reveal three distinct thematic clusters: (1) blockchain’s foundational role in marketing operations and advertising systems; (2) ethical considerations, trust-building, and decentralized consumer relationship management; and (3) immersive consumer engagement through the metaverse and digital technologies. The research also synthesizes the key theoretical frameworks driving the field, specifically the Theory of Planned Behavior, Social Exchange Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Value Co-creation Theory. By identifying critical gaps such as cross-platform behavioral dynamics, the long-term sustainability of gamified loyalty, and equitable stakeholder governance, this paper establishes a conceptual framework designed to guide both scholarly investigation and managerial implementation in the decentralized digital economy.

latest.title: Coping with sustainability information overload: The role of generative artificial intelligence literacy
latest.venue: Ho Chi Minh City Open University Journal of Science- Economics and Business Administration
latest.abstract: Consumers can use sustainability information to consume responsibly; however, excessive and complex sustainability claims might confuse consumers and hinder proper evaluations. Based on cognitive appraisal theory, this study empirically investigates the impacts of sustainability information overload (SIO) on green information avoidance (GIA) and green information verification behavior (GIVB) and examines the moderating role of generative AI literacy (GAIL) and the associations of GIA and GIVB with green purchase decision confidence (GPDC). Data from an online cross-sectional survey of 468 adult consumers in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings revealed that SIO positively influenced GIA, and GIA negatively influenced GPDC. However, SIO did not negatively influence GIVB on average. GAIL significantly moderated the SIO-GIVB relationship: SIO was negatively associated with GIVB at low GAIL but not significantly at mean or high GAIL.GIVB positively influenced GPDC. An indirect effect of SIO on GPDC through GIA is significant, but the indirect effect through GIVB is not significant unconditionally. These results suggest that sustainability information overload is associated with distinct coping responses. From a practical perspective, sustainability portals and shopping applications involving GenAI should emphasize evaluability and verifiability rather than enhancing disclosures. Through defining GAIL as a digitally mediated capability from the consumer’s perspective which can serve as a coping tool, this paper builds on cognitive appraisal theory in the context of AI-mediated sustainable consumption and explains the critical engagement of consumers with sustainability information amid overload situations

latest.title: Generative Ai-Enabled Financial Forecasting and Strategic Financial Decision Quality in Emerging-Market SMEs
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study investigates how generative AI enabled financial forecasting capability and business analytics capability shape strategic financial decision quality in emerging market SMEs, with particular attention to the moderating role of AI governance maturity. Grounded in organizational information processing theory and dynamic capabilities theory, the study argues that better financial decisions depend not simply on access to advanced technologies, but on how effectively firms turn AI generated forecasts and analytical information into useful financial judgment. AI governance maturity is expected to strengthen this process by providing appropriate oversight, accountability, validation, and control over the use of AI generated financial information. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 385 respondents who possessed relevant knowledge of SME financial management, business analytics, AI applications, or organizational decision making. Data were collected using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed with IBM SPSS version 26. Reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and multiple linear regression were performed, while Hayes’ Process Macro Model 1 was used to test the moderating effect. The results show that generative AI enabled financial forecasting capability (β = 0.613) and business analytics capability (β = 0.487) both have significant positive effects on strategic financial decision quality. AI governance maturity also strengthens the relationship between generative AI enabled financial forecasting capability and strategic financial decision quality, with an interaction coefficient of 0.518. These findings suggest that emerging market SMEs gain greater value from generative AI when forecasting tools are supported by sound ana

latest.title: AI as corporate communicator: the role of AI source transparency, trust, and engagement in brand advocacy
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) as a corporate communicator and examines how AI source transparency influences message credibility, employee trust, employee engagement and ultimately brand advocacy. Specifically, the study explores both cognition-based and affect-based dimensions of trust and evaluates the moderating role of AI literacy in shaping employees’ responses to AI-generated communication. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted using an online survey questionnaire. Data were collected from 317 employees across different organizations who had experience with AI-mediated communication in their workplace. Structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0 was applied to test the proposed relationships and evaluate the conceptual framework. Findings The findings indicate that AI source transparency positively affects message credibility. Message credibility significantly enhances both cognition-based and affect-based trust, which subsequently increase employee engagement. Employee engagement was also found to positively influence brand advocacy. However, AI literacy showed an unexpected negative moderating effect on the relationship between message credibility and cognition-based trust, suggesting that employees with greater AI knowledge become more critical and skeptical of AI-generated content, whereas its moderating effect on the relationship between message credibility and affect-based trust is not statistically significant. Practical implications Organizations should not use AI solely as an automation tool but also as a strategic communication instrument. Transparency regarding AI usage, combined with human oversight and quality assurance mechanisms, can strengthen credibility and t

latest.title: The impact of environmental knowledge on water waste in restaurants on complaining behavior intention: The mediating role of perceived motivation and skepticism
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of environmental knowledge about water waste in restaurants on consumers' intentions to complain, while also elucidating the mediating roles of perceived motivation and skepticism in this relationship. A scenario-based experimental research design was employed, and data were gathered from 388 restaurant goers through an online survey. Participants were randomly assigned to two restaurant scenarios: one in which water-saving practices were not observable and another in which they were prominently displayed. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analyses in SPSS 26 and AMOS 23. The research findings demonstrate that, in the first scenario—characterized by the absence of visible communication about water conservation—environmental knowledge had no direct, significant influence on the intention to display complaint behavior. Environmental knowledge increased perceived motivation and skepticism. Perceived motivation did not directly and significantly influence the intention to engage in complaint behavior; however, skepticism increased the intention to engage in such behavior. In the second scenario, where water-saving methods were visible, environmental knowledge directly and positively affected the intention to complain, perceived motivation, and skepticism; furthermore, perceived motivation and skepticism partially mediated the relationship between environmental knowledge and the intention to complain. The findings suggest that restaurants must not only implement eco-friendly practices but also communicate them to consumers in a transparent, visible, and trustworthy way. In this context, restaurant managers should create informative visuals and communication strategies that promote water

latest.title: A Case Study of Dabur India's Digital Transformation Balancing data-driven intelligence, organisational agility and human judgement
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing how organisations interpret information, anticipate business conditions and make decisions. In fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), decisions concerning demand, marketing, distribution, procurement and operations require timely information and coordinated responses. This case study examines Dabur India Limited’s digital transformation initiatives and their managerial implications, with emphasis on AI-enabled analytics, data integration, business visibility and human oversight. The study adopts a qualitative case-study design based on publicly available secondary sources, including company disclosures, corporate announcements and academic literature. It analyses the strategic context of Dabur’s cloud modernisation and announced AI-led enterprise transformation, and considers potential applications across sales, marketing, supply chain, finance and procurement. The discussion identifies opportunities associated with faster access to information, improved coordination and data-informed planning, alongside challenges involving data quality, employee readiness, governance, accountability and overreliance on automated outputs. Because some AI initiatives are announced or planned, the study distinguishes reported developments from intended outcomes and does not claim independently measured performance effects. It argues that AI is best understood as a managerial decision-support capability whose value depends on organisational readiness, critical interpretation and responsible implementation.

Impact of perceived social risk on the tendency toward sports gambling addiction among Chinese recreational sports club members: verifying the mediating effect of sports values
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examines the associations between perceived social risk and the tendency toward sports gambling addiction among recreational sports club members in China, with particular attention to the potential indirect role of sports values. Drawing on general strain theory and psychosocial value frameworks, perceived social risk is conceptualized as a multidimensional perception of economic, interpersonal, psychological, and physical pressures in everyday social and recreational contexts, while the COVID-19 period is treated as contextual background rather than as part of the construct itself. Methods Using data from 362 recreational sports participants with previous sports lottery purchasing experience, the study employed confirmatory factor analysis, multiple regression, and bootstrap mediation analysis. Results Economic, psychological, and interpersonal risks were positively associated with gambling tendency, whereas physical risk was not significant. In the parallel multiple-mediator models, the total indirect effect through the five sports-value dimensions was significant for economic, interpersonal, and psychological risk, but not for physical risk. Among the 20 specific indirect effects, only the pathway from interpersonal risk through character values to gambling tendency had a 95% bootstrap confidence interval that excluded zero. Discussion The findings provide exploratory evidence concerning the relationships among perceived social risk, sports values, and gambling tendency in this sample, while highlighting the need for longitudinal and cross-cultural research with more representative samples.

latest.title: Blockchain capability and knowledge transfer in sustainability-oriented supply chain financing: evidence from Saudi Arabia
latest.abstract: Introduction Blockchain-enabled supply chain financing depends not only on verifiable digital records but also on organizational capabilities that convert distributed information into usable knowledge and financing decisions. This study examines the associations among knowledge transfer (KT), sustainable supply chain (SSC) practices, perceived organizational blockchain capability (BC), and supply chain financing (SCF) in Saudi Arabia. Methods A quantitatively dominant cross-sectional design used 210 usable survey responses analyzed through an integrated partial least squares path model and was complemented by 13 semi-structured managerial interviews. The simultaneous model estimated the direct, indirect, and interaction relationships among KT, SSC practices, BC, and SCF. Results KT was positively associated with SSC practices (β = 0.602, p < 0.001) and SCF (β = 0.307, p < 0.001), while SSC practices were positively associated with SCF (β = 0.344, p < 0.001). The specific KT → SSC → SCF indirect effect was significant (β = 0.207, BCa 95% CI [0.139, 0.282]). BC also showed a positive direct association with SCF (β = 0.322, p < 0.001). The BC × KT interaction was small and non-significant (β = 0.021, p = 0.583, BCa 95% CI [−0.051, 0.095]). The integrated model explained 36.2% of SSC variance and 65.2% of SCF variance. Discussion The findings distinguish blockchain’s direct information value from the stronger proposition of capability complementarity. Knowledge transfer is associated with financing both directly and indirectly through SSC practices, while BC contributes a distinct positive association with SCF but does not significantly strengthen the KT–SCF relationship in this sample. Managerial interview evidence contextualizes these findings through transparency, coordi

latest.title: INTEGRATION PROCESSES AS A MEANS OF IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF CUSTOMER SERVICE IN HOTEL BUSINESSES
latest.abstract: The article provides a comprehensive theoretical and practical substantiation of integration processes within the hotel and restaurant industry as a foundational strategic vector for enhancing service quality, operational efficiency, and overall competitiveness. Amidst escalating market globalization and shifting consumer expectations, modern hospitality enterprises must transition from isolated accommodation providers to dynamic, multi-functional ecosystem models capable of delivering holistic, highly personalized guest experiences. The study investigates the profound impacts of digital integration, specifically focusing on the implementation of state digital infrastructure tools (such as Ukraine’s "Diia" document-sharing service) to streamline check-in workflows, eliminate paper-based archives, and significantly reduce administrative friction. Furthermore, the research examines the architectural synthesis of core internal operational systems—including Property Management Systems (PMS), Point of Sales (POS), Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Online Reputation Management (ORM), Internet of Things (IoT), and dynamic pricing engines—underpinned by robust cybersecurity and data protection frameworks. It is demonstrated that dismantling managerial fragmentation through a unified technological ecosystem resolves systemic inefficiencies, safeguards sensitive personal data, and curates seamless guest journeys. Beyond digital paradigms, the article explores non-digital horizontal and vertical integration strategies through the metamorphosis of traditional hotels into complex mixed-use developments that amalgamate residential, commercial, coworking, gastronomic, wellness, and cultural functions. The findings substantiate that establishing such multi-functional complexes en

latest.title: Brand recommendations by generative AI chatbots: A comparative analysis in consumer decision-making
latest.abstract: This study explored the algorithmic gatekeeping role of generative AI chatbots in consumer decision-making. Using algorithmic content analysis and an audit design, it examined the brand recommendations of the three most widely used chatbots in Türkiye: ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. Four product categories were selected by crossing involvement level and consumption motivation: detergent, chocolate, smartphone and an international holiday. Each prompt was submitted once to each model in a neutral and an emotional version, and the resulting 24 responses were coded descriptively. Neutral prompts mostly elicited technical and functional arguments, whereas emotional wording shifted the persuasion frame toward emotional appeals in 8 of 12 responses; predominantly emotional responses appeared only in hedonic categories. In the holiday category, all three models framed even the neutral prompt in romantic terms. The models typically offered three to ten brands rather than a single one, yet ChatGPT stated a first-person preference in every response and displayed priced shopping cards in five of eight. The findings suggest that generative AI can act as an intermediary that shapes brand visibility and has the potential to steer consumer preferences, raising questions for marketing ethics and large language model optimization.

latest.title: Content dynamics and their impact on sponsorship efficiency in digital sports broadcasting: a comparative visual exposure analysis via PSG–Bayern Munich and Atletico Madrid–Arsenal matches
latest.venue: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
latest.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the associations between content dynamics and sponsorship efficiency in digital sports broadcasting using a computer vision-based approach and to present a comparative exploratory analysis across two distinct European cup matches. The research adopts a computational content analysis method and a comparative multiple case study design. Within the scope of the study, the official match recordings of the Paris Saint-Germain FC – Bayern Munich (April 28, 2026) and Atlético Madrid – Arsenal FC (April 29, 2026) matches broadcasted on the YouTube platform were analyzed. Sponsorship visibility was examined on a per-second basis using a custom AI-driven computer vision algorithm developed in the MATLAB environment, which integrated the Region of Interest (ROI) technique to evaluate in-screen brand density, temporal exposure duration, and spatial positioning parameters. The research findings demonstrate that the sponsorship visibility performance index tends to reach significantly higher levels in matches characterized by high in-game action and tempo. Specifically, sponsorship visibility was found to peak during critical offensive sequences and goal moments, whereas close-up shots and replay sequences were associated with temporary drops in visibility. In the high-action intensity match, the maximum sponsorship visibility index reached a peak score of 1,446 points, whereas the maximum efficiency score in the lower-tempo, highly controlled match was found to be 23.93% lower. Furthermore, it was observed that camera angles, close-ups, and replay sequences preferred by the broadcasting director exhibit strong associations with the screen persistence and visual exposure potential of brands within this two-match observation. Working With Robots: How Robot Proportion in Human-Robot Teams and Robot Anthropomorphism Shape Employee Turnover Intention
latest.abstract: Although robots are increasingly reshaping organizational workflows, how the robot proportion in human-robot teams affects employees’ turnover intention remains underexplored. Drawing on conservation of resources theory, we examine whether, why, and when robot proportion exerts divergent effects on turnover intention through two pathways: resource gain and resource loss. Evidence from a scenario-based experiment (Study 1, N = 290) and a three-wave field study (Study 2, N = 306) reveals that these two pathways operate in opposing directions. Specifically, work goal progress and work loneliness mediate the relationship between robot proportion in human-robot teams and turnover intention. Robot anthropomorphism further moderates these pathways: higher anthropomorphism strengthens the beneficial effect on work goal progress, whereas lower anthropomorphism amplifies the detrimental effect on work loneliness. This study offers initial evidence on how the structural composition of human-robot teams shapes employees’ turnover intention, and it provides practical implications for organizations deploying robotic coworkers.

latest.title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

latest.title: ESG Performance and Corporate Market Value: A Study Based on Indonesian Listed Companies
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: Under the dual pressures of global sustainability and emerging market transformation, the impact of ESG performance on corporate value has become a key academic and practical concern. Using panel data of 339 Indonesian listed firms (3,381 observations) from 2016 to 2025, this study employs two-way fixed-effects models, instrumental variables, and mediation analysis to investigate the effect, heterogeneity, and mechanisms of ESG on market value. The results show that: (1) ESG performance has a significant and robust positive effect on market value. This finding holds after multiple robustness checks and remains significant after addressing endogeneity. (2) This effect is heterogeneous. It is stronger for SMEs and high-profitability firms, positive for non-polluting firms, but negative for polluting firms. (3) Mechanism tests reveal that ESG enhances market value indirectly by improving corporate liquidity (current ratio) and core profitability (operating margin). By providing micro-level evidence from Indonesia, this study enriches the literature on ESG's heterogeneous effects in emerging markets. The findings offer empirical guidance for firms' differentiated ESG strategies, investors' portfolio construction, and regulators' policy design.

latest.title: Electronic Word of Mouth, Brand Image, and Brand Trust on Brand Loyalty Mediated by Consumer Satisfaction
latest.abstract: Purpose— To examine the relationships of electronic word of mouth (e-WOM), brand image, and brand trust with loyalty among Telkomsel users in Solo Raya, and the statistical mediating role of customer satisfaction. Research Methodology— Data from a cross-sectional online questionnaire completed by 300 purposively recruited Telkomsel users were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4.0. Results— e-WOM, brand image, and brand trust showed positive associations with satisfaction. Brand image, brand trust, and satisfaction were positively associated with loyalty, whereas the direct e-WOM–loyalty relationship was not statistically significant. All three indirect paths through satisfaction were positive and significant. Research limitations/Implications— Nonprobability recruitment, a cross-sectional self-report design, and inconsistent measurement indices constrain generalization and statistical interpretation. Reliable services and responsive complaint handling should accompany digital marketing efforts. Originality— The study jointly examines three antecedents and a satisfaction-mediated association in a regional mobile-telecommunications setting, with complaint handling represented within the satisfaction measure.

latest.title: Smart supply chain and sustainable competitive advantage: role of operational ambidexterity, green new product development and green operation
latest.venue: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
latest.abstract: Purpose The main aim of this research is to adopt practices that can help manufacturers reduce the material footprint of companies and, then, nations. We first show that when each firm configures a smart supply chain, it can significantly enhance its green performance metrics and achieve a better position in a dynamic market. With the help of a smart supply chain, companies can reduce emissions, increase the recycling process of materials and reduce the consumption of rare resources or environmentally harmful items. Design/methodology/approach In the present research, structural equation modeling was used, and SmartPLS was utilized to analyze all postulated correlations between the constructs. We assess the constructs' validity and reliability in the measuring model. We use Cronbach's alpha and composite reliability to assess the internal consistency reliability of the construct measures in the SmartPLS software. Findings Managers focus on enhancing the competencies and skills of their workforce to effectively manage both smart supply chain initiatives and green new product development. Operational ambidexterity can provide information for training programs to bridge knowledge gaps and equip employees with the necessary skills. Originality/value This research will help policymakers and researchers understand the critical role of variables as a guiding principle in driving the successful implementation of sustainable practices within the intersections of smart supply chains. Moreover, organizations can enhance their competitive advantage, economic performance and environmental stewardship in an increasingly resource-constrained world.

latest.title: Exploring the Integration of Cloud Technologies with Oracle ERP Systems: Benefits and Opportunities
latest.venue: Frontiers in Emerging Computer Science and Information Technology
latest.abstract: Cloud technologies are increasingly becoming transformational to the business enterprise with the issues of flexibility, scalability and data-driven decisions. A combination of cloud solutions and Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems is now an important idea to organizations that seek to enhance operational efficiency, workflows and real-time insight into business. In this paper, the integration of cloud technologies into Oracle ERP examined with the deployment models, the service frame and the enabling technology/tools like REST and SOAP APIs, Oracle Integration Cloud and pre-built adapters considered. Observed industry practice indicates that cloud-based Oracle ERP makes collaboration, automation, cost optimization, enhanced security and compatibility with emerging technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), low-code/no-code platforms, IoT and blockchain simpler. The review of the current practices sheds some light on the most widespread spheres of implementation issues, such as data migration, customization, and system implementation, as well as usability difficulties, integration issues, and problems. It provides some ideas concerning the approaches that might be considered to guarantee effective adoption. As this paper argues, cloud ERP implementations and integration, together with case studies in organizations, reveal the potential of cloud-powered ERP systems as strategic enablers of digital transformation, business resiliency and long-term innovation. Additionally, future trends have been of interest in the study of AI-based predictive analytics, self-adaptive ERP, and cross-industry comparative modeling to optimize cloud ERP adoption and enhance competitive edge in businesses.

latest.title: Organisational Kinetics: Toward A General Theory of Responsiveness and Organisational Change
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: In today’s dynamic business climate, organisations face technological disruptions, digital transformation, intense competition, globalisation and shifting stakeholder expectations, which compel them to renew their plans, strategies, structures and behaviours continually. Existing perspectives, such as dynamic capabilities, organisational agility, organisational learning and absorptive capacity, offer insights into aspects of adaptation but leave room for explaining the transition from collective understanding to coordinated action. This conceptual paper proposes an approach called organisational kinetics to explain how organisations generate, coordinate and sustain purposeful motion. Drawing on organisational cognition, dynamic capabilities and adaptive systems perspectives, the framework conceptualises organisations as dynamic systems whose responsiveness depends on five interconnected dimensions. Organisational organic cognition enables organisations to sense and interpret their environment, learn from it and formulate adaptive responses; adaptive velocity relates to the speed of response; communication flow facilitates the sharing and integration of knowledge; structural flexibility enables organisational adjustment; and energetic alignment promotes commitment and collective action towards strategic goals. The paper presents organisational kinetics as an integrative approach that examines the speed, intensity, direction and effective coordination of firms’ responses and pursuit of their goals. Based on this analysis, it concludes that organisational kinetics provides an integrated framework for exploring differences in organisational responsiveness under similar environmental conditions. It therefore suggests empirical studies to validate the framework’s dimensions,

latest.title: Emotion regulation and venture performance: evidence from rural entrepreneurship
latest.abstract: Introduction Rural entrepreneurs are constrained by resource shortages and institutional barriers, and are prone to experiencing persistent emotional stress. However, existing research has not fully clarified the mechanism by which emotion regulation affects venture performance. Most related studies have focused on urban entrepreneurs, lacking comparative analysis of the mediating roles of explorative learning and exploitative learning, and failing to clearly define the boundary role of entrepreneurial experience. Based on this, drawing on upper echelons theory and Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this paper explores the mechanism of emotion regulation and venture performance among rural entrepreneurs, analyzes the mediating roles of explorative learning and exploitative learning, and empirically examines the moderating effect of entrepreneurial experience. Methods We adopted a two-wave time-lagged survey design to mitigate common method bias, collecting valid questionnaires from 207 Chinese rural entrepreneurs. A series of validity and data screening checks were implemented to ensure the rigor of the analysis. Hierarchical regression analysis was employed to test the main effects and moderating effects, while the bootstrap method was applied to examine the mediating effects and to compare the relative strength of the two mediating pathways. All analyses were conducted using SPSS 21 and Amos 22. Results Emotion regulation is positively related to venture performance. Both exploitative learning and explorative learning mediate the relationship between emotion regulation and venture performance. We also find that the positive effect of emotion regulation on venture performance mainly operates through the channel of explorative learning. Moreover, the study finds th

latest.title: Nghiên cứu thực nghiệm đánh giá mức độ ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo trong việc cá nhân hóa trải nghiệm du khách tại thành phố Đà Nẵng
latest.abstract: Trong bối cảnh chuyển đổi số đang tái định hình ngành du lịch toàn cầu, trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) ngày càng trở thành một công nghệ chiến lược trong phát triển du lịch thông minh. Tuy nhiên, các nghiên cứu hiện nay chủ yếu tập trung vào hiệu quả ứng dụng công nghệ hoặc hành vi chấp nhận công nghệ, trong khi cơ chế tác động của AI đến hành vi hậu trải nghiệm của du khách, đặc biệt là ý định quay lại điểm đến, vẫn chưa được làm rõ tại các thị trường mới nổi như Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện nhằm phân tích cơ chế tác động của các yếu tố thuộc hệ sinh thái AI đến trải nghiệm du lịch thông minh, niềm tin công nghệ và ý định quay lại của du khách tại Đà Nẵng. Nghiên cứu được xây dựng trên nền tảng tích hợp giữa Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Service-Dominant Logic (SDL) và Trust Theory, từ đó đề xuất mô hình nghiên cứu gồm năm biến công nghệ thế hệ mới: AI Personalization, AI Interactivity, Predictive Intelligence, Data Privacy Assurance và Immersive Technology Integration. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp hỗn hợp, bao gồm nghiên cứu định tính thông qua phỏng vấn chuyên gia nhằm hiệu chỉnh thang đo và nghiên cứu định lượng thông qua khảo sát 400 khách du lịch nội địa và quốc tế đã trải nghiệm dịch vụ tại Đà Nẵng. Dữ liệu được phân tích bằng IBM SPSS Statistics và SmartPLS thông qua các kỹ thuật Cronbach’s alpha, EFA, CFA, SEM và Bootstrapping. Kết quả nghiên cứu kỳ vọng sẽ chứng minh rằng các yếu tố AI không chỉ nâng cao trải nghiệm du lịch thông minh mà còn góp phần hình thành niềm tin công nghệ và thúc đẩy hành vi quay lại điểm đến. Nghiên cứu được kỳ vọng đóng góp về mặt lý luận thông qua việc mở rộng các mô hình hành vi công nghệ trong bối cảnh du lịch thông minh; đồng thời cung cấp cơ sở thực tiễn cho doanh nghiệp và cơ quan quản lý trong việc xây dựng chiến lược

latest.title: Make or buy? A CIO’s framework for adopting foundation models in the enterprise
latest.abstract: Although make-or-buy decisions are well established in operations and information technology management, the emergence of foundation models introduces challenges that existing frameworks only partially address. Prior research on AI-specific make-or-buy decisions remains limited, leaving organizations with insufficient guidance for sourcing foundation models. This study addresses this gap by developing a structured make-or-buy decision framework for foundation models following the design science research paradigm. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and Transaction Cost Economics, the framework is informed by a systematic literature review and 13 expert interviews and is evaluated through a naturalistic case-based study with five organizations. The resulting artifact links strategic objectives with operational feasibility and extends classical make-or-buy frameworks to the context of foundation models. Beyond the specific instantiation, we derive general design principles for future make-or-buy decision artifacts for foundation models. Overall, the study contributes to theory by operationalizing and extending established sourcing perspectives in an emerging technological context and to practice by providing a structured tool for reassessing foundation model sourcing strategies.

latest.title: Who chose the label? Voluntary versus mandated AI disclosure in tourism marketing
latest.abstract: Generative AI is being used extensively by destination marketing organisations (DMOs) to create promotional imagery, and new regulation requires disclosure of some synthetic content. Previous research indicates that revealing an AI source can reduce perceived authenticity but treats disclosure as a single cue. This study investigated whether travellers react differently when the AI label is presented as the DMO's own decision or as a legally mandated requirement. A simulated single factor, three condition (no label, voluntary label, mandated label) between-subjects online experiment with N = 387 adult participants. The analysis was based on the Persuasion Knowledge Model and attribution theory, using ANCOVA, bootstrapped parallel mediation analyses (multicategorical predictor), moderation by attitudes towards AI and robustness checks. Both labels reduced perceived authenticity compared to no label (voluntary: d = −0.59; mandated: d = −0.74). The voluntary label raised perceived DMO integrity (d = 0.38), producing a positive indirect effect on visit intention. The mandated label earned no integrity credit, and its negative indirect effect through authenticity was not compensated. These effects were not significantly moderated by general attitudes toward AI. The study distinguishes between what the AI label says and who is seen to have chosen it, thereby furthering the research on persuasion-knowledge in tourism and providing a model that DMOs can test for disclosure in the regulatory era.

latest.title: From Triple Bottom Line (TBL) to Supply Chain Triple Value Bottom Line (SCTVBL): A Sustainable Supply Chain Value Framework
latest.abstract: In today's competitive business environment where consumers increasingly expect transparency, quality, and value for money, buying a product means interacting with the entire supply chain. As the modern supply chains become more autonomous and interconnected, the effective measurement of their business value necessitates transitioning from the conventional efficiency‐based business models to more holistic, stakeholder‐focused business models. In this regard, although the triple bottom line (TBL) framework offers sustainability of the supply chains via economic, social, and environmental performance dimensions, it does not segregate and comprehensively capture value for the key supply chain stakeholders, thereby disregarding the important stakeholders like employees, customers, suppliers, and partners. Therefore, by evaluating the gaps in the extant supply chain management literature coupled with analyzing, critiquing, and synthesizing the current supply chain performance frameworks, and drawing upon the guiding theories, this research introduces a novel concept, “supply chain triple value bottom line” (SCTVBL), and subsequently presents a SCTVBL framework. While addressing the evolving performance needs of the contemporary supply chains, the proposed framework further extends the conventional TBL framework by offering value‐oriented supply chains perspective. As a whole, by suggesting organizational value creation (via economic value, operational value, and employee value), socio‐environmental value creation (via social value and environmental value), and relational value creation (via customer value and supplier & partner value) as renewed supply chain value dimensions, the SCTVBL framework offers a more stakeholder‐focused perspective for holistically addressing the v

latest.title: Beyond resistance: deinfluencing, consumer activism and the incorporation of critique on digital platforms
latest.abstract: Deinfluencing is a social media trend where content creators advise audiences not to buy ‘must-have,’ overhyped, overpriced, low-quality, or unnecessary products. It serves as a potential form of resistance to the logic of overconsumption. Gaining momentum on TikTok in early 2023, deinfluencing rapidly spread across social media platforms where the meanings and norms of consumption are publicly negotiated and can acquire collective relevance. This conceptual paper proposes a critical reading of the phenomenon, arguing that deinfluencing does not necessarily constitute a negation of influencer marketing, but may instead be incorporated into the commercial arrangements it contests while retaining critical meanings and effects. Situated at the intersection of consumer culture, consumer activism, influencer marketing and platformisation, the paper examines the infrastructural and commercial conditions through which consumer critique acquires visibility and value. It develops a multilevel conceptual model comprising three analytically distinct but potentially overlapping mechanisms through which critical discourse can be incorporated into influencer marketing: substitution , at the content level, whereby criticism of particular products redirects rather than rejects consumption; hybridisation , at the level of practices, whereby influencing and deinfluencing coexist within creators’ communicative repertoire; and authenticity renewal , at the level of audience relations, whereby rejecting some products can strengthen creator credibility and, under certain conditions, the persuasive value of subsequent endorsements. Platformisation conditions the circulation and visibility of these critical practices without determining their effects. Drawing on the sociological concept of bou

latest.title: Beyond Operational Fluency: A Three-Tier AI Literacy Architecture for Reskilling and Upskilling in Strategic Talent Development
latest.venue: International Journal of AI in Pedagogy Innovation and Learning Futures
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) occupies two positions in talent development simultaneously: the principal driver of the reskilling imperative, obsoleting skills faster than organizations can replace them, and increasingly the instrument through which reskilling is delivered, via adaptive platforms, generated content, and automated coaching. Reskilling scholarship assumes training technology is causally independent of the skill shift it responds to, an assumption prior industrial transitions permitted but AI's shared mechanism no longer does. This conceptual paper argues that AI's dual position generates five failure modes conventional reskilling models cannot detect: velocity without capability, a deskilling loop in which the instrument reproduces the condition it was deployed to remedy, personalization that fragments collective capability, stratified access that widens the divide reskilling was meant to close, and erosion of the entry-level roles through which experiential learning occurs. Drawing on integrative reviews of AI and workers' skills, Industry 4.0 reskilling blueprints, and AI governance scholarship, the paper applies the HUMAN framework (Human Oversight, Upskilling for AI Literacy, Meaningful Augmentation, Accountability and Audit, Networked Learning) to each failure mode, and extends its upskilling principle into a three-tier AI literacy architecture, operational fluency, evaluative literacy, and complementary capability, that depreciates at rates inverse to the investment it typically attracts. The paper translates this into five testable propositions and offers implementation guidance differentiated by organizational context.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The Role of Emotional Attachment in Mediating the Influence of Parasocial Interaction on Impulsive Buying (Study on BTS Fans in Denpasar City)
latest.abstract: The growing popularity of the Korean Wave (Hallyu) in recent years has contributed to increased consumption of South Korean popular culture products, particularly Korean pop (K-pop), across various countries, including Indonesia. The global popularity of BTS has fostered strong emotional connections between fans and their idols through digital interactions on social media platforms. These interactions may facilitate the development of parasocial relationships and emotional attachment, potentially influencing fans' consumption behavior, including impulsive buying. This study aimed to examine and explain the mediating role of emotional attachment in the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying among BTS fans, collectively known as ARMY, in Denpasar City, Indonesia. The study population comprised BTS fans residing in Denpasar City, from whom 120 respondents were selected using a nonprobability purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.0. The findings revealed that parasocial interaction had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and emotional attachment. Furthermore, emotional attachment had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and partially mediated the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying. These findings highlighted the importance of parasocial interaction and emotional attachment in explaining impulsive buying tendencies among BTS fans. The study provided insights into the psychological mechanisms underlying fan consumption behavior and offered practical implications for marketers seeking to understand consumer engagement and purchasing decisions within digital fa

latest.title: ДОСЛІДЖЕННЯ СВІТОВИХ ТРЕНДІВ РОЗВИТКУ РЕКЛАМИ В УМОВАХ ЗАСТОСУВАННЯ ІНФОРМАЦІЙНИХ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ: ОСОБЛИВОСТІ ЇХ ВИКОРИСТАННЯ В УКРАЇНІ
latest.abstract: У статті проведено дослідження сучасних тенденцій розвитку світового рекламного ринку та особливостей їх застосування в Україні. Проаналізовано динаміку світового рекламного ринку та визначено посилення ролі цифрової реклами. Проаналізовано рівень ринкової капіталізації провідних рекламних компаній світу та встановлено значну концентрацію капіталу серед найбільших учасників ринку. Систематизовано ключові світові рекламні тренди. На прикладі світових компаній досліджено практичне застосування сучасних рекламних технологій у діяльності міжнародних компаній. Окрему увагу приділено рекламному ринку України. Виявлено активне впровадження світових рекламних трендів українськими компаніями. Запропоновано підхід до формування рекламної стратегії української компанії в умовах обмеженого бюджету.

latest.title: A Comparative Analysis of Customer Segmentation Techniques Using K-Means, Hierarchical and Density-Based Spatial Clusterings
latest.venue: Jharkhand Journal of Development and Management Studies
latest.abstract: In present day data driven marketing process customer segmentation is very important component so that institutions may understand diverse client behavior and undertake design inspired initiatives. With growing availability of transactional data, artificial intelligence (AI) -based unsupervised learning techniques have gained popularity for identifying meaningful customer segments without prior labeling. This study presents a comparative analysis of three commonly used approaches to customer segmentation such as K-Means clustering, Hierarchical clustering, and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN). This study is based on the data set taken from Kaggle consisting of 541,909 records and eight variables. The customer label data which is aggregated from transaction-level to construct behavioral features based on Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM). Along with additional purchase behavior indicator to assess transaction and principal component analysis (PCA) was applied prior to clustering for high scale sensitivity and high dimensionality. Study results showed that K-Means offer well separated stable clusters of large customer groups. Hierarchical clustering offers valuable insights into cluster structures and DBSCAN nicely diagnosed noise and atypical purchasing behavior at the same time sensitive to parameter selection in high density marketing data. The study showcased the trade-offs between algorithmic performance as well as business interpretability, giving guidance to marketing analysts enabling decision-makers to decide suitable segmentation techniques.

latest.title: The Influence of AI-Driven Conversational Commerce on Electric Vehicle Customer Satisfaction and Repeat Purchase Intention in Pune District, Maharashtra (2023–24 to 2025–26)
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven conversational commerce—comprising multilingual Natural Language Processing (NLP) chatbots, WhatsApp Business API assistants, voice-enabled in-app concierges, and predictive Customer Relationship Management (CRM) interfaces—in shaping customer satisfaction (CSAT) and repeat purchase intention (RPI) among Electric Vehicle (EV) consumers across Pune District, Maharashtra, from FY 2023–24 to FY 2025–26. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) frameworks, the research combines longitudinal secondary registration data from Maharashtra Vahan portals and the Pune Regional Transport Office (RTO) with a structured primary survey of N = 420EV owners across urban, peri-urban, and rural talukas (Pune City, Haveli, Pimpri-Chinchwad, Mulshi, Maval, Baramati, Shirur, and Daund). Statistical analysis using Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, and one-way ANOVA demonstrates that conversational responsiveness, personalized Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) estimation, and predictive service reminders significantly elevate customer satisfaction (R2 = 0.684, p < 0.001), which in turn strongly mediates repeat purchase and brand advocacy intention (β = 0.742, p < 0.001). However, algorithmic opacity in complex battery-warranty disputes and data privacy concerns remain notable friction points, particularly in semi-urban corridors.

latest.title: Sensor-wide association studies: a methodological architecture for developing and evaluating functional human traits
latest.abstract: Background Wearable and other digital sensors enable longitudinal observation of physiology and behaviour. However, reproducible associations and predictive performance do not establish which physiological construct a sensor-derived representation measures. An explicit framework is needed to distinguish statistical representation, construct interpretation and mechanistic explanation. Objective This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes Functional Human Traits (FHTs) and Sensor-Wide Association Studies (SWAS) as a conceptual and methodological architecture for developing and evaluating individual-level representations of physiological response capacities. Conceptual framework An FHT is defined as a quantitative representation of a specified physiological response capacity, supported by temporal repeatability over a justified interval and independent biological evidence under stated conditions. SWAS links documented sensor features, exploratory analysis, candidate construction and independent evaluation. Outcome-guided screening estimates feature–outcome associations, whereas unsupervised analysis identifies statistical structure; neither directly identifies a physiological construct. Candidate construction requires an explicit measurement model, individual-level estimation with uncertainty and tests addressing competing interpretations. Evaluation distinguishes statistical replication, technical robustness, temporal repeatability and biological support. A hypothetical cardiovascular heat-response example illustrates candidate construction using a longitudinal model. Environmental sensing and semantic integration are optional supporting components where relevant to the research question. Implications SWAS integrates established association-study and sensor-based measurem

latest.title: Pandemic crisis and the race for supply chain resilience through organizational learning and agility
latest.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed deep structural vulnerabilities in global supply chains (SC) and demonstrated the importance of resilience as a capability for adaptive continuity under prolonged disruption. This study examines how organizational learning (OL) and organizational agility (OA) were associated with resilience-related SC responses during large-scale disruption, with particular attention to digitally enabled coordination. Drawing on a multiple case study of seven European firms and 17 semi-structured interviews, the study provides qualitative evidence on how firms developed crisis preparedness, adaptive response, and recovery capabilities during the pandemic. The case findings associated structured training, crisis reflection, cross-functional learning, employee empowerment, and the knowledge-sharing routines with preparedness and adaptive SC responses. Accounts of agility emphasized rapid decision-making, responsive communication, process reconfiguration, and technology-enabled coordination under conditions of supply shortages, logistics disruptions, and demand volatility. Across the cases, digital coordination, timely information sharing, and technology-enabled communication were described as supporting resilience-related SC responses across interconnected supply networks. Theoretically, the paper advances the SCR literature by explaining how OL and OA operate as interrelated organizational mechanisms that support resilience-related supply chain responses during prolonged disruption. Managerially, the findings suggest that firms should institutionalize learning routines, deepen collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, and invest in digital capabilities that support agile communication, visibility, and coordination during future crises.

latest.title: AI-Powered Smart Society: How Technology is Transforming Consumer Behavior, Marketing and Operations

Mechanisms underlying the role of digital and intelligent mental health services in relation to suicidal ideation among college students: a chain mediation model involving crisis perception and psychological resilience
latest.abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of global digital transformation and increasing psychological stress among college students, suicidal ideation has emerged as a significant public health concern. Digital and intelligent mental health services, characterized by accessibility, anonymity, and convenience, have become an important complement to traditional mental health service models. However, the psychological mechanisms underlying the association between digital and intelligent mental health service use and suicidal ideation remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between digital and intelligent mental health service use and suicidal ideation among college students and to examine the mediating roles of crisis perception and psychological resilience. Methods Based on the interaction perspective of stress and cognition and positive psychology theory, a cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 1,086 undergraduate students from a university in Shandong Province using cluster sampling. Participants completed measures assessing digital and intelligent mental health service use, crisis perception, psychological resilience, and suicidal ideation. SPSS 26.0 was used to conduct common method bias tests and correlation analyses, and Model 6 of the PROCESS macro was employed to examine the chain mediation model. Results Digital and intelligent mental health service use was significantly and negatively associated with suicidal ideation (β = −0.315, p < 0.001). Mediation analyses revealed three significant indirect pathways: the independent mediating effect of crisis perception, the independent mediating effect of psychological resilience, and the chain mediating effect involving crisis perception and psychological resilience.

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms.
