latest.title: PENGARUH ELECTRONIC WORD OF MOUTH (eWOM) TERHADAP MINAT BELI MELALUI FEAR OF MISSING (FOMO) PADA PARFUM MYKONOS DI TIKTOK
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menguji pengaruh electronic word of mouth (eWOM) terhadap minat beli parfum Mykonos di TikTok, dengan menempatkan fear of missing out (FOMO) sebagai variabel mediasi. Penelitian dilakukan dengan pendekatan kuantitatif dan melibatkan 155 pengguna TikTok yang mengetahui parfum Mykonos serta pernah melihat informasi atau konten mengenai produk tersebut. Responden ditentukan melalui purposive sampling sesuai dengan kriteria penelitian. Data yang terkumpul selanjutnya diolah menggunakan Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui SmartPLS 4.Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa eWOM berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap minat beli maupun FOMO, sementara FOMO juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap minat beli serta terbukti memediasi pengaruh eWOM terhadap minat beli. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa eWOM mampu mendorong minat beli parfum Mykonos, baik secara langsung maupun melalui terbentuknya FOMO, sekaligus memberikan implikasi bagi Mykonos dalam mengelola eWOM dan mengembangkan strategi pemasaran melalui TikTok.

latest.title: ProactiMate: evaluating LLM-based chatbots for behavior change interventions
latest.abstract: This paper explores the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in promoting sustainable behavior, specifically in overcoming procrastination. Despite widespread recognition of the need for sustainable behavior change, individuals often struggle to break free from entrenched, unsustainable habits. LLMs, such as OpenAI’s GPT-4, represent a significant breakthrough in artificial intelligence and are increasingly used in behavior change interventions. This study introduces ProactiMate, a chatbot built using Motivational Interviewing (MI) principles and a Chain of Models approach for prompt engineering, designed to help users combat procrastination. Our research compares four LLMs (GPT-3.5 Turbo, LLaMA-3.2, Qwen-2.5, and SmolLM-1.7B) for output influence on procrastination avoidance, and assesses the impact of hyperparameters (temperature and top-p values) on procrastination avoidance. The findings reveal that GPT-3.5 outperforms other models across various evaluation metrics, and higher temperature and top-p values lead to more effective procrastination avoidance from automatic evaluation. According to expert evaluations, Qwen-2.5 and GPT-3.5 Turbo demonstrated notable effectiveness in fostering user engagement and motivation for addressing procrastination, with GPT-3.5 Turbo particularly distinguished by its capacity to provide strategies that help maintain long-term motivation. And GPT’s output aligns well with both automatic evaluation metrics and human evaluation. The results provide insights into the most effective ways to use LLMs in chatbot design, offering solutions for future usability testing.

latest.title: Line curvilinearity–masculinity associations on packaging influence expected taste intensity of green tea
latest.abstract: Despite the growing global popularity of green tea, the intensity of its taste varies due to differences in cultivation environments and processing methods. According to crossmodal sensory theory, other senses often interact with taste to shape taste expectations and thereafter flavour perception, with visual cues playing a particularly important role. This research investigated the impact of line curvilinearity (Angular vs. Rounded) on expected taste intensity in the context of green tea packaging and further explored its underlying mechanisms through the lens of perceived femininity and masculinity. This research demonstrated across three experiments that angular (vs. rounded) lines enhanced the expected taste intensity in green tea packaging (Studies 1-3), ultimately leading to increased willingness to purchase (Study 2-3). Specifically, the stronger the expected taste of green tea, the greater the willingness to purchase. Furthermore, angular (vs. rounded) lines were more strongly associated with perceived masculinity (vs. femininity). Notably, perceived masculinity led consumers to expect that the tea would have a more intense taste, whereas perceived femininity did not have the same effect. This suggests that perceived masculinity mediates the relationship between line curvilinearity and expected taste intensity (Studies 1-3). These findings therefore provide insights for tea enterprises in terms of optimizing packaging design and potentially enhancing their social media marketing strategies.

latest.title: Building Customer Loyality for Marning Corn in Bulukumba: The Impact of Brand Image, Service Quality, and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions and Customer Satisfaction
latest.venue: Journal of Global Innovations in Agricultural Sciences
latest.abstract: Marning corn products, typical food, and souvenirs from the Bulukumba district are packaged simply without complete product information. Yet by integrating well-designed packaging with clear and relevant product information that can improve product quality, brands can improve the overall consumer experience, build trust, and foster long-term loyalty. This research aims to analyze the direct and indirect influence of brand image, service quality, and product quality on purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction on consumer loyalty to making corn. The research method used quantitative analysis with structured interview techniques using a sample of corn buyers in Bulukumba Regency. The data analysis used is structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis using the AMOS application. The research results show that consumer satisfaction and brand image have a significant direct influence on loyalty. Brand image and service quality have an impact on purchasing decisions. Product quality, service quality, and brand image influence consumer satisfaction. Meanwhile, the variables of service quality and production quality do not have a significant effect on consumer loyalty through purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction as intervening variables of brand image, service quality, and production quality. Increasing income in the Morning Corn business can be achieved by prioritizing brand image, service quality, and product quality so that later it can increase the number of buyers and increase consumer loyalty. Keywords: Customer loyalty, buying decision, customer satisfaction, brand image, service quality, product quality and marning corn.

latest.title: A bibliometric and content analysis of marketing in Web 3.0
latest.abstract: The transition to Web 3.0 driven by blockchain, non-fungible tokens (NFTs), and the metaverse presents a transformative paradigm shift for digital marketing. Yet, the current body of academic research remains notably fragmented. This study systematically maps the intellectual structure of Web 3.0 marketing to consolidate existing knowledge, uncover dominant trends, and propose a cohesive agenda for future research. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a comprehensive bibliometric and content analysis of 121 documents from the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection spanning 2009 to 2025. Leveraging analytical tools including Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CitNetExplorer, the study maps citation networks, keyword co-occurrences, and bibliographic coupling. The findings demonstrate an exponential surge in academic interest starting in 2021 and reveal three distinct thematic clusters: (1) blockchain’s foundational role in marketing operations and advertising systems; (2) ethical considerations, trust-building, and decentralized consumer relationship management; and (3) immersive consumer engagement through the metaverse and digital technologies. The research also synthesizes the key theoretical frameworks driving the field, specifically the Theory of Planned Behavior, Social Exchange Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Value Co-creation Theory. By identifying critical gaps such as cross-platform behavioral dynamics, the long-term sustainability of gamified loyalty, and equitable stakeholder governance, this paper establishes a conceptual framework designed to guide both scholarly investigation and managerial implementation in the decentralized digital economy.

latest.title: Strategi Komunikasi Coffee Shop Goodhands dalam Menarik Minat Konsumen
latest.abstract: Persaingan usaha Coffee Shop menuntut pelaku usaha menerapkan strategi komunikasi pemasaran yang efektif untuk menarik perhatian dan meningkatkan minat kunjungan konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis strategi komunikasi Coffee Shop Goodhands dalam menarik minat konsumen berdasarkan model AISAS (Attention, Interest, Search, Action, dan Share). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif. Informan berjumlah enam orang yang terdiri atas satu pemilik usaha, dua karyawan, dan tiga konsumen yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi nonpartisipan, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model Miles dan Huberman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tahap Attention dibangun melalui konten visual Instagram yang menampilkan produk, suasana, dan kegiatan Goodhands. Tahap Interest didukung oleh kualitas produk, konsep interior bergaya vintage, pelayanan, dan kegiatan live music. Pada tahap Search, Instagram menjadi sumber informasi mengenai menu, harga, lokasi, dan kegiatan. Tahap Action dipengaruhi oleh promosi, rekomendasi teman, serta pengalaman konsumen, sedangkan tahap Share terlihat melalui unggahan dan rekomendasi langsung. Namun, tahap Action dan Share belum berjalan optimal. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa Goodhands perlu memperkuat konsistensi konten, promosi kegiatan, dan keterlibatan konsumen untuk meningkatkan efektivitas komunikasi serta minat kunjungan.

latest.title: Analisis Pendekatan Personal Selling Beauty Advisor Berbasis Skin Analysis terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen pada Toko Ettra Kosmetik
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi dan Manajemen Indonesia
latest.abstract: Persaingan industri kosmetik dan skincare mendorong toko ritel menghadirkan layanan yang lebih personal bagi konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan dan menganalisis pendekatan personal selling Beauty Advisor berbasis skin analysis serta kaitannya dengan keputusan pembelian konsumen pada Toko Ettra Kosmetik. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi non-partisipatif, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi selama Praktik Kerja Lapangan pada 31 Agustus sampai 20 November 2026, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa personal selling dijalankan secara konsultatif, adaptif, dan berorientasi pada hubungan, mulai dari approach, identifikasi kebutuhan, presentasi produk dengan tester, penanganan keberatan, closing yang tidak agresif, hingga follow-up. Skin analysis memperkuat tahap identifikasi kebutuhan sehingga rekomendasi produk disesuaikan dengan kondisi kulit, usia, kebiasaan perawatan, dan anggaran konsumen. Kendala utama meliputi ketidaksediaan sebagian konsumen menjalani skin analysis, toko yang ramai, dan ketidaktersediaan stok produk yang direkomendasikan. Penelitian ini belum membuktikan hubungan sebab-akibat antara skin analysis dan keputusan pembelian.

latest.title: Slow travel from a positive psychology perspective
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
latest.abstract: This study examines the concept of slow travel from the perspective of positive psychology. In this context, the Touristic Eastern Express, one of the most prominent examples of tourist rail travel in Türkiye, was analyzed through the vignette technique (short narratives), and the effects of slow travel on individuals’ psychological well-being were explored. The findings indicate that slow travel fosters positive interpersonal relationships, enhances individuals’ meaning-making processes, and supports self-awareness and personal development. Furthermore, this type of travel contributes to the emergence and sustainability of positive emotions. Slow travel also enables individuals to engage more deeply with their surroundings, offering a reflective and immersive travel experience. In this regard, it provides opportunities to experience key psychological processes such as mindfulness, flow, and empowerment. Through these processes, slow travel offers more meaningful and fulfilling experiences, ultimately contributing to increased levels of happiness, subjective well-being, and overall life satisfaction.

latest.title: Social media, brand image, and price perception as predictors of purchase decisions: Evidence from kopi kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia
latest.venue: The Contrarian Finance Accounting and Business Research
latest.abstract: This study examines whether social media, brand image, and price perception are associated with the purchase decisions of Kopi Kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia, a regional market in which prior findings for this brand are mixed. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 100 customers, recruited through purposive sampling offline and online, was analyzed with multiple linear regression. Social media and brand image were positively and significantly associated with purchase decisions, with effects of comparable and moderate size. Price perception showed no significant association, and its confidence interval included zero, so no direction of effect can be inferred. Together, the three predictors explained about one quarter of the variance in purchase decisions. The study provides jointly estimated effects, confidence intervals, and effect sizes for three commonly studied predictors in an Eastern Indonesian city. Informative social media content and a consistent brand image are associated with purchase decisions, whereas the study offers no evidence for or against a price-perception association. Non-probability sampling, a single time point, self-reported data, and modestly reliable price and purchase-decision scales limit generalization.

latest.title: Tinjauan Kritis Model Lima Kekuatan Porter untuk Teknologi Additive Manufacturing: Perspektif Ekonomi Industri dan Metodologi Penelitian
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi dan Manajemen Indonesia
latest.abstract: This study presents a critical review of the article by Soraya Dias, Pedro Espadinha-Cruz, and Florinda Matos (2023) entitled "A Porter’s Five Forces Model Proposal for Additive Manufacturing Technology: A Case Study in Portuguese industry" in Procedia Computer Science (Vol. 217, pp. 165–176). Evaluated through research methodology and industrial organization economics, this review examines the validity and economic logic of adapting Porter’s Five Forces to Additive Manufacturing (AM) across 13 Portuguese firms. Methodologically, the study exhibits a mismatch between its claimed qualitative exploratory case study design and its execution as a descriptive web survey without thematic coding or inferential testing. Severe selection bias arises because 12 of 13 firms use AM only as an auxiliary prototyping tool (61% report zero final-product weight), alongside contradictions between tables and text (notably the 92% AM knowledge access figure in Table 5 and cross-table misreferencing). Economically, the authors conflate a production process technology with a distinct market boundary, overlooking marginal cost trade-offs between economies of scale and scope, oligopolistic supplier concentration versus low switching costs, labor market friction, and public-good externalities in unprotected intellectual property rights (IPR).

latest.title: Does CEO regulatory focus shape firms’ international diversification? Exploring the moderating role of marketing and corporate governance
Coping with sustainability information overload: The role of generative artificial intelligence literacy
latest.venue: Ho Chi Minh City Open University Journal of Science- Economics and Business Administration
latest.abstract: Consumers can use sustainability information to consume responsibly; however, excessive and complex sustainability claims might confuse consumers and hinder proper evaluations. Based on cognitive appraisal theory, this study empirically investigates the impacts of sustainability information overload (SIO) on green information avoidance (GIA) and green information verification behavior (GIVB) and examines the moderating role of generative AI literacy (GAIL) and the associations of GIA and GIVB with green purchase decision confidence (GPDC). Data from an online cross-sectional survey of 468 adult consumers in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings revealed that SIO positively influenced GIA, and GIA negatively influenced GPDC. However, SIO did not negatively influence GIVB on average. GAIL significantly moderated the SIO-GIVB relationship: SIO was negatively associated with GIVB at low GAIL but not significantly at mean or high GAIL.GIVB positively influenced GPDC. An indirect effect of SIO on GPDC through GIA is significant, but the indirect effect through GIVB is not significant unconditionally. These results suggest that sustainability information overload is associated with distinct coping responses. From a practical perspective, sustainability portals and shopping applications involving GenAI should emphasize evaluability and verifiability rather than enhancing disclosures. Through defining GAIL as a digitally mediated capability from the consumer’s perspective which can serve as a coping tool, this paper builds on cognitive appraisal theory in the context of AI-mediated sustainable consumption and explains the critical engagement of consumers with sustainability information amid overload situations

latest.title: Peran Literasi Digital dan Sistem Informasi Manajemen dalam Memediasi Hubungan Transformasi Digital dengan Kinerja Keuangan UMKM
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of digital transformation on the financial performance of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through digital literacy and management information systems as mediating variables. The study employed a quantitative approach involving 150 MSME owners as respondents. Data were collected through five-point Likert-scale questionnaires and analyzed using the Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) method with the assistance of SmartPLS software. The results indicate that digital transformation has a positive and significant effect on digital literacy (β = 0.477), management information systems (β = 0.544), and financial performance (β = 0.247). Furthermore, digital literacy (β = 0.192) and management information systems (β = 0.336) have positive and significant effects on MSME financial performance. The mediation test results demonstrate that digital literacy and management information systems mediate the relationship between digital transformation and MSME financial performance. These findings confirm that digital transformation not only has a direct impact but also contributes to improving MSME financial performance through enhanced digital literacy and the utilization of management information systems.

latest.title: Tata Kelola Memoderasi Dalam Meningkatkan Sustainability Di Era Digital
latest.venue: Jurnal Agregasi Aksi Reformasi Government dalam Demokrasi
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine whether Digitalization and Income Tax Incentives influence the Sustainability of MSMEs, moderated by good governance. A sample of 325 MSME respondents was selected. Data were obtained through questionnaires and analyzed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach with the assistance of SmartPLS 4 software. The analysis was conducted on survey data from 325 MSME respondents using a bootstrapping technique for 5,000 subsamples. The findings indicate that digitalization and income tax incentives influence MSME Sustainability, and good governance, as a moderating variable, does not strengthen the influence of digitalization and income tax incentives on MSME Sustainability. The contribution of this study is that, armed with capital savings from income tax incentives and sales volume driven by digitalization, MSMEs can adapt to market changes, increase resilience, and ensure long-term business continuity.

latest.title: The role of incentive mechanisms and intellectual property awareness in retaining R&D personnel in Chinese biopharmaceutical companies: the mediating role of perceived R&D staffing adequacy
latest.abstract: Retaining research and development (R&D) personnel is a strategic challenge for Chinese biopharmaceutical companies because innovation depends on cumulative knowledge, long project cycles, and stable interdisciplinary teams. This study examines how career satisfaction, incentive mechanisms, intellectual property awareness, psychological contract fulfillment, and team collaboration influence R&D personnel retention, with perceived R&D staffing adequacy as a structural mediator. Data were obtained from 650 valid questionnaires collected from R&D employees in 27 biopharmaceutical companies; 900 questionnaires were distributed, yielding a 72.2% valid response rate. Regression, mediation, and firm-size subgroup analyses were conducted. The results show that all five antecedents are positively associated with retention. Career satisfaction has the strongest direct association, followed by psychological contract fulfillment, incentive mechanisms, intellectual property awareness, and team collaboration. Perceived staffing adequacy significantly transmits the associations of career satisfaction and incentive mechanisms with retention, while the continuing significance of the corresponding direct paths is consistent with partial mediation. Firm-size comparisons suggest that career satisfaction, incentives, and staffing adequacy are more salient in small and medium-sized enterprises, whereas intellectual property awareness is more salient in large enterprises. The findings extend strategic human resource management research by connecting motivational, relational, intellectual-property, and workforce-planning mechanisms in an innovation-intensive setting.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Generational differences in quiet quitting: Exploring presenteeism and job burnout among hotel employees
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationships between quiet quitting, presenteeism, and burnout among hotel employees, based on Generation Theory and Conservation of Resources (COR) theory. It also aims to determine whether quiet quitting levels differ across generations. Data were collected from employees of 5-star hotels operating in Türkiye using a survey, a quantitative data collection method. The findings show a positive relationship between quiet quitting and presenteeism, and between presenteeism and job burnout. Furthermore, hotel employees across Generations X, Y, and Z differ significantly in their perceptions of quiet quitting. The present study offers recommendations for HR managers and practitioners to reduce employee turnover in the hospitality industry.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Gender stereotypes and portrayals in advertising: implications for emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals in advertising shape early-stage emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults. It positions gendered advertising as both a branding issue and a responsible-marketing concern in youth-oriented marketplaces. Design/methodology/approach A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 159 valid responses from a Vietnamese sample concentrated mainly in the younger age segment; 83.6% of respondents were aged 14–26. Skincare and automobile advertising stimuli were used to manipulate stereotype congruity and the gender of the focal protagonist. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed relationships. Findings Both gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals significantly influence emotional brand attachment across the experimental conditions. Emotional brand attachment, in turn, positively predicts brand sacredness and its three dimensions: communitas, supremacy and mesmerization. The findings are interpreted as immediate relational and symbolic responses within a youth- and young-adult-oriented sample, not as evidence of fully matured brand attachment or sacredness. Originality/value This study contributes to young-consumer and gender-in-advertising research by extending attention from proximal persuasion outcomes to early relational and symbolic brand outcomes. It clarifies the conceptual distinction between gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals and explains how these cues may shape early-stage attachment and sacredness-related perceptions among young consumers and young adults. The findings also offer responsible-marketing implications: although gendered portrayals may strengthen consumer–brand

latest.title: Determinan Minat Investasi Reksadana Pendapatan Tetap Syariah pada Generasi Produktif Kota Jambi
latest.abstract: Public interest in Islamic investment has continued to grow; however, participation in Islamic fixed-income mutual funds remains relatively low compared to other Islamic investment instruments. This condition highlights the need to identify the factors influencing public interest in investing in this financial product. This study aims to examine the effects of return perception, risk perception, and Islamic financial literacy on investment interest in Islamic fixed-income mutual funds among the productive-age population in Jambi City, Indonesia. A quantitative approach with a survey method was employed, involving 101 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics 26. The results indicate that return perception and Islamic financial literacy have a positive and significant effect on investment interest, whereas risk perception has a negative and significant effect. Simultaneously, the three independent variables significantly influence investment interest, with an Adjusted R Square value of 0.490, indicating that the model explains 49.0% of the variance in investment interest, while the remaining 51.0% is attributable to factors outside the proposed model. These findings underscore the importance of strengthening Islamic financial literacy, improving public perceptions of potential investment returns, and fostering a balanced understanding of investment risk to enhance public interest in Islamic fixed-income mutual funds.

latest.title: Live Streaming Commerce and Impulse Buying Behavior: A Literature Review
latest.abstract: Live streaming commerce (LSC) has accelerated impulsive purchasing, yet the literature mostly examines what triggers purchases and rarely addresses how impulses are regulated and what follows after the transaction. This article maps recent evidence on impulse buying in LSC and proposes a conceptual framework linking triggers to consequences. An integrative literature review was conducted on 29 reputable sources, focusing on 2019–2026 studies: 17 empirical or analytical studies, eight reviews, and four conceptual or methodological references. The synthesis shows that research is dominated by Stimulus–Organism–Response models that end at impulsive buying intention or behavior, whereas self-regulation and post-purchase consequences are seldom tested, particularly in the Indonesian context. As a conceptual contribution, the article proposes a Stimulus–Organism–Regulation–Consequence (S-O-R-C) framework that positions regulation as a gatekeeping stage and consequences as a cyclical feedback loop, accompanied by six testable propositions. Future research should adopt longitudinal or field-experimental designs on Shopee Live and TikTok Live and measure regret, returns, and consumer well-being.

latest.title: AI as corporate communicator: the role of AI source transparency, trust, and engagement in brand advocacy
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) as a corporate communicator and examines how AI source transparency influences message credibility, employee trust, employee engagement and ultimately brand advocacy. Specifically, the study explores both cognition-based and affect-based dimensions of trust and evaluates the moderating role of AI literacy in shaping employees’ responses to AI-generated communication. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted using an online survey questionnaire. Data were collected from 317 employees across different organizations who had experience with AI-mediated communication in their workplace. Structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0 was applied to test the proposed relationships and evaluate the conceptual framework. Findings The findings indicate that AI source transparency positively affects message credibility. Message credibility significantly enhances both cognition-based and affect-based trust, which subsequently increase employee engagement. Employee engagement was also found to positively influence brand advocacy. However, AI literacy showed an unexpected negative moderating effect on the relationship between message credibility and cognition-based trust, suggesting that employees with greater AI knowledge become more critical and skeptical of AI-generated content, whereas its moderating effect on the relationship between message credibility and affect-based trust is not statistically significant. Practical implications Organizations should not use AI solely as an automation tool but also as a strategic communication instrument. Transparency regarding AI usage, combined with human oversight and quality assurance mechanisms, can strengthen credibility and t

latest.title: The impact of environmental knowledge on water waste in restaurants on complaining behavior intention: The mediating role of perceived motivation and skepticism
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of environmental knowledge about water waste in restaurants on consumers' intentions to complain, while also elucidating the mediating roles of perceived motivation and skepticism in this relationship. A scenario-based experimental research design was employed, and data were gathered from 388 restaurant goers through an online survey. Participants were randomly assigned to two restaurant scenarios: one in which water-saving practices were not observable and another in which they were prominently displayed. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analyses in SPSS 26 and AMOS 23. The research findings demonstrate that, in the first scenario—characterized by the absence of visible communication about water conservation—environmental knowledge had no direct, significant influence on the intention to display complaint behavior. Environmental knowledge increased perceived motivation and skepticism. Perceived motivation did not directly and significantly influence the intention to engage in complaint behavior; however, skepticism increased the intention to engage in such behavior. In the second scenario, where water-saving methods were visible, environmental knowledge directly and positively affected the intention to complain, perceived motivation, and skepticism; furthermore, perceived motivation and skepticism partially mediated the relationship between environmental knowledge and the intention to complain. The findings suggest that restaurants must not only implement eco-friendly practices but also communicate them to consumers in a transparent, visible, and trustworthy way. In this context, restaurant managers should create informative visuals and communication strategies that promote water

latest.title: Financial Literacy Calibration and Retail Investor Behavior on Digital Trading Platforms: A Literature Review
latest.abstract: The number of young retail investors in Indonesia has surged while capital market literacy remains low, making the role of financial literacy in curbing investor bias a central issue in financial management. This article maps evidence on financial literacy, self-confidence, and retail investor behavior on digital trading platforms and proposes a conceptual framework. An integrative literature review was conducted on 29 sources: 18 empirical or analytical studies, seven reviews or meta-analyses, two theoretical or methodological references, and two contextual data sources. The synthesis shows that the role of literacy in reducing bias is not uniform because it depends on the type of bias and on how literacy is measured; confidence in one's own knowledge can raise market participation as well as trading intensity; and platform design shapes behavior, especially among investors with low literacy. As a conceptual contribution, the article proposes a Literacy–Confidence–Platform (L-K-P) framework centered on the calibration gap between objective literacy and confidence, accompanied by six testable propositions. Future research should combine objective literacy tests with actual transaction data and field experiments on investment platforms in Indonesia.

latest.title: A Case Study of Dabur India's Digital Transformation Balancing data-driven intelligence, organisational agility and human judgement
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing how organisations interpret information, anticipate business conditions and make decisions. In fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), decisions concerning demand, marketing, distribution, procurement and operations require timely information and coordinated responses. This case study examines Dabur India Limited’s digital transformation initiatives and their managerial implications, with emphasis on AI-enabled analytics, data integration, business visibility and human oversight. The study adopts a qualitative case-study design based on publicly available secondary sources, including company disclosures, corporate announcements and academic literature. It analyses the strategic context of Dabur’s cloud modernisation and announced AI-led enterprise transformation, and considers potential applications across sales, marketing, supply chain, finance and procurement. The discussion identifies opportunities associated with faster access to information, improved coordination and data-informed planning, alongside challenges involving data quality, employee readiness, governance, accountability and overreliance on automated outputs. Because some AI initiatives are announced or planned, the study distinguishes reported developments from intended outcomes and does not claim independently measured performance effects. It argues that AI is best understood as a managerial decision-support capability whose value depends on organisational readiness, critical interpretation and responsible implementation.

latest.title: Antecedents and Consequences of Follower Gratitude in the Context of Influencer Marketing
Youth engagement with algorithmic consumerism cultures: A systematic psychological review.
latest.abstract: This article presents a systematic literature review and a conceptual framework for understanding how youth engage with and are influenced by algorithmic consumerism cultures on social media. We integrate findings from 72 quantitative , experimental, and qualitative psychological studies to examine a relatively new form of consumer culture that has been advanced by social media and algorithmic technologies, in which novel marketing methods and the strategic targeting of youth through social media influencers are increasingly prevalent. We conceptualize this as algorithmic consumerism cultures that are unique in their pace, individualization , user engagement, and implicitness. The results show that youth engagement with consumerism online is shaped by three main psychological processes: intrapersonal processes influencing identity and well-being , social processes influencing motivation and persuasion , and cognitive and moral developmental processes influencing critical engagement and advertising literacy . Advancing this field requires methodologies that capture the reciprocal influence between algorithm-driven consumerist content on social media and youth’s active navigation of this content. This requires conceptualizing such spaces as subcultures with their own norms and practices that need to be investigated through the perspectives of the “ natives ” of those cultures: youth.

latest.title: A Study on Lead Management and Customer Engagement Practices in the Residential Real Estate Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Residential real estate is a high-involvement purchase in which customers generally compare several projects, evaluate affordability and consult family members before making a decision. For a channel partner, the quality of lead management and customer engagement therefore plays an important role in moving an enquiry towards a site visit and, ultimately, a booking. This paper examines the lead management and customer engagement practices observed at Thee House Of Real Estate Solutions Pvt. Ltd., Pune, during the internship undertaken by Om Sunil Tiwari. The study follows a descriptive and exploratory approach. Primary information was drawn from participant observation, customer requirement calls, follow-up activities, property presentations, virtual interactions, site-visit coordination and discussions with the sales team. Secondary information was drawn from project brochures, available sales material and relevant concepts of customer relationship management, relationship marketing and consumer buying behaviour. The analysis is qualitative because detailed company-wide conversion statistics and complete commercial records were not available. The observations indicate that lead conversion is influenced by the quality of the initial enquiry, accurate understanding of customer requirements, clarity of pricing and project information, timely follow-up, product knowledge and coordination for site visits. Customers evaluate properties on factors such as budget, location, configuration, purchase purpose, possession expectations and developer credibility. The paper recommends structured lead qualification, updated customer records, planned follow-up, personalised communication and verified property information. The findings are specific to the internship experience and should

latest.title: Determinants of Insurance Operational Efficiency Perception under Inclusive Digital Transformation: A Case Study of Digitalization at A Insurance Company Guangxi , China
latest.venue: Journal of Frontier in Economic and Management Research
latest.abstract: The objectives of this research were to 1) examine the current level of customer- perceived operational efficiency, and 2) analyze the effects of intelligent underwriting, online claims processing, digital marketing, digital transformation, and data analytics capability on this efficiency at A Insurance Company in Guangxi, China. This quantitative study collected data from 356 customers, selected through a two- stage sampling procedure combining simple random sampling at the company level and stratified random sampling by prefecture-level cities at the customer level. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, content validity analysis (IOC), Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression analysis. The research findings revealed that 1) despite the complete digital service modules established by Company A, a substantial proportion of respondents rarely utilized digital insurance tools, indicating a gap between digital infrastructure development and actual user adoption. 2) All five digitalization-related factors exerted significant positive effects on customer-perceived operational efficiency, with online claims processing demonstrating the strongest predictive effect while data analytics capability showed relatively weaker though still significant influence. The regression model achieved satisfactory explanatory power, and the measurement scales demonstrated satisfactory reliability and content validity, with all five research hypotheses supported.

latest.title: From sustainability practices to consumer behaviour: a PLS-SEM analysis of sustainable packaging adoption in the FMCG food sector
latest.abstract: Growing environmental concerns and plastic waste are driving the need for sustainable packaging solutions for the FMCG food sector. Understanding consumer attitude and purchasing behavior for sustainably packaged food products is crucial for promoting sustainable practices. This study assesses the association between the 5R's sustainability practices, consumer attitude, purchase intention, and actual purchasing behavior towards sustainably packaged FMCG food products. Primary data were collected from 210 consumers using the purposive sampling method from various hypermarkets in Coimbatore city. The data were analysed by Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling with SmartPLS 4 software. From the results, it is revealed that 5R sustainability practices significantly influence consumer attitude (β = 0.730) towards sustainably packaged food products. Furthermore, consumer attitude has a positive influence on purchase intention (β = 0.666), whereas purchase intention considerably influences actual purchasing behavior (β = 0.543). However, the direct association between attitude and actual purchasing behavior was not significant (β = −0.115), indicating the existence of an intention–behavior gap in sustainable consumption. The structural model explains 53.3% of the variance in attitude, 44.4% in purchase intention, and 22.5% in actual purchasing behavior, highlighting that purchase intention acts as a key mediating factor between attitude and actual behavior. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening consumer intention and improving the availability of sustainably packaged food products to enhance actual purchasing behaviour

latest.title: Digital Advertising and Brand Awareness among Consumers in Enugu State, Nigeria
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The study examined the relationship between digital advertising and brand awareness among consumers in Enugu State, Nigeria. Specifically, the study sought to examine the relationship between social media advertising and brand recognition and determine the relationship between search engine advertising and brand recall among consumers in Enugu State. The study was conducted in Enugu Metropolis, Enugu State, using a descriptive survey research design. Primary data were collected through the administration of questionnaires. The study had a total population of 999 respondents, from which a sample size of 278 was determined using Freund and Williams' statistical formula at a 5% margin of error. Of the 278 questionnaires distributed, 222 were returned and correctly completed. The data collected were presented and analyzed, while the hypotheses were tested using the Z-test statistic. The findings revealed that social media advertising had a significant positive relationship with brand recognition among consumers in Enugu State (Z = 8.121, p < 0.05). Similarly, search engine advertising had a significant positive relationship with brand recall among consumers in Enugu State (Z = 8.289, p < 0.05). The study concluded that digital advertising has a significant positive relationship with brand awareness among consumers in Enugu State, Nigeria. The study recommended, among other things, that businesses should intensify their social media advertising activities through platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and WhatsApp to improve brand visibility.

latest.title: Product Packaging Design and Buying Behavior of Shoe Retail Consumers
latest.venue: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
latest.abstract: Product packaging design is an important element of product presentation that may influence consumers’ perceptions and purchasing decisions. However, limited research has examined the relationship between product packaging design and buying behavior among shoe retail consumers in the Philippine retail context, particularly in Davao City. This study examined the level of product packaging design and buying behavior among shoe retail consumers, determined whether significant differences existed in these variables when grouped according to monthly income, and assessed the relationship between product packaging design and buying behavior. A quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive-correlational-comparative research design was employed. The study involved 200 shoe retail consumers selected through convenience-quota sampling, with 50 participants assigned to each of four monthly income groups. Data were collected using a validated structured questionnaire and analyzed using mean, standard deviation, analysis of variance, and Pearson correlation. Results showed that product packaging design was at a very high level (m=3.71), while buying behavior was likewise at a very high level (m=3.70). No significant difference was found in product packaging design across income groups (p=.150). Similarly, buying behavior did not significantly differ across income groups (p=.075). However, a strong positive and statistically significant relationship was found between product packaging design and buying behavior, with a correlation coefficient of r=.822 and a probability value of p<.001. The findings indicate that consumers generally perceive shoe packaging favorably and demonstrate strong buying behavior regardless of income group. The strong association between packaging design and buy

latest.title: Rural Market Activation, Retailer Engagement and Distribution Development in the FMCG Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Rural and semi-urban markets represent an important opportunity for fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies, but effective market development depends on more than product availability. Retailer relationships, local market understanding, systematic outlet coverage, competitive observation and dependable distribution all influence whether products reach consumers. This paper presents a field-based, descriptive and exploratory study of the Haat Project undertaken by the researcher during an On-the-Job Training (OJT) engagement with ITC Limited in the Nagpur Region from 18 May 2026 to 18 July 2026. The project involved field exposure in Nashirabad, Shendurni, Pahur, Bodwad, Faizpur, Muktainagar and Savda. Activities included market mapping, retailer and wholesaler interaction, retail audits, product and stock observation, competitor monitoring, retailer addition, order booking, distribution follow-up and collection of market feedback. The study focuses on ITC products including Sunfeast YiPPee!, Mom’s Magic, Mom’s Magic Shine and Marie Light. The available project record supports qualitative analysis of market conditions, retailer requirements and the field sales process; it does not provide a verified consolidated sample size or complete outlet-wise numerical dataset. Accordingly, the paper does not present invented counts, percentages or causal claims. The findings indicate that rebuilding retailer confidence, improving product availability, maintaining regular market coverage and aligning product offerings with local demand are important priorities for rural FMCG development. The paper concludes with practical recommendations for strengthening retailer engagement, market intelligence and distribution coordination. Keywords: FMCG, rural marketing, market activation, r

latest.title: Environmental Considerations and Performance of Agricultural Firms in Kiambu County, Kenya
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Agricultural firms in Kiambu County play a significant role in Kenya's economy through their contribution to agricultural production, employment, and livelihoods. However, these firms continue to experience performance challenges associated with operational inefficiencies, resource wastage, declining profitability, and environmental risks. Despite the growing emphasis on environmental sustainability, the extent to which environmental considerations influence the performance of agricultural firms remains insufficiently established. Therefore, this study sought to examine the influence of environmental considerations on the performance of agricultural firms in Kiambu County, Kenya. Specifically, the study focused on eco-friendly products, environmental regulatory compliance, carbon footprint management, and environmental audits. The study was anchored on the Triple Bottom Line Theory and adopted an explanatory research design. The unit of analysis comprised 200 registered agricultural firms in Kiambu County, while the unit of observation consisted of heads of procurement, finance, operations, quality assurance, and marketing departments. The target population comprised 1,250 departmental heads, from whom a sample of 305 respondents was selected using Slovin's formula. Stratified random sampling was employed to ensure representation of the respective departmental categories. Primary data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires. A pilot study involving 31 departmental heads from agricultural firms in Murang'a County was conducted to assess the validity and reliability of the research instrument. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, while quantitative data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 28 through descriptiv

latest.title: The Influence of Live Streaming on Purchasing Decisions for Glad2glow Products among Tiktok Shop Users in Grade Xii at SMA Daarul Muttaqien Tangerang
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of live streaming on purchasing decisions for Glad2Glow products among Grade XII students at SMA Daarul Muttaqien Tangerang who use TikTok Shop. A quantitative associative approach was employed, involving 42 respondents selected through purposive sampling from a population of 60 students. The respondents were selected based on their experience watching Glad2Glow live streaming and purchasing its products through TikTok Shop. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using IBM SPSS version 26 through simple linear regression. The results indicate that live streaming has a positive and significant influence on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.221, a t-value of 3.220, and a significance level of 0.003. The coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.206 indicates that live streaming explains 20.6% of the variation in purchasing decisions, while the remaining 79.4% is attributable to factors outside the research model. These findings suggest that live streaming is one of the factors associated with consumers' purchasing decisions for Glad2Glow products.

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
