hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: AI and employee wellbeing in the workplace: An empirical study
hot.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace settings significantly affects employees, particularly their wellbeing. Despite its growing relevance, the impact of AI on employee wellbeing remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a survey and employed structural equation modeling to analyze data from Finnish and international companies headquartered in Finland (n = 207). We found that AI adoption does not directly impact employee wellbeing but indirectly influences it through work-related factors of task optimization and safety. This highlights the importance of strategically implementing AI to enhance aspects of work that are important to employees, thereby maximizing the wellbeing benefits of AI adoption. Practically, this study underscores the need for AI adoption to result in tangible improvements in organizational tasks and processes, data security, and occupational health. When these aspects are adequately addressed, AI adoption can enhance employee wellbeing and contribute to improved human-AI integration in the workplace.

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: Strategic human resource management in the digital economy era: an empirical study of challenges and opportunities among MSMEs and startups in Indonesia
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies on workforce productivity and organizational performance within Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and startups in Indonesia. Anchored in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the research conceptualizes digital HRM as a strategic asset that enhances organizational performance by enabling firms to develop, deploy, and reconfigure human capital capabilities in response to digital transformation. The conceptual model includes five constructs: Digital Technology Adoption in HRM, Digital Training and Development, Work Flexibility and Hybrid Management, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention, and Utilization of HR Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to MSME and startup leaders and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with Smart PLS. The results indicate that Digital Technology Adoption, Digital Training and Development, and Work Flexibility do not significantly influence workforce productivity or organizational performance (p > 0.05). However, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention and the Utilization of HR Analytics and AI have a significant and positive impact on both workforce productivity and performance outcomes (p = 0.000). These findings highlight that while not all digital HR strategies yield immediate benefits, the ability to build dynamic capabilities through innovative talent practices and data-driven HR systems is essential to achieving competitive advantage and organizational success in the digital economy.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Barriers and Enablers of AI Adoption in Human Resource Management: A Critical Analysis of Organizational and Technological Factors
hot.abstract: This paper examines the key factors recognized as transformative in the field of human resource management (HRM) and explores their influence on the global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). While AI holds significant promise for enhancing HRM efficiency, employee engagement, and Decision Making, its implementation presents a range of organizational, technical, and ethical challenges that organizations worldwide must navigate. Change aversion, data security worries, and integration expenses are major roadblocks, but strong digital leadership, company culture, and advancements in NLP and machine learning are key enablers. This paper presents a complex analysis that questions the common perception of AI as only disruptive by delving into the relationship between power dynamics, corporate culture, and technology infrastructures. In this paper, we bring together research from several fields to help scholars and practitioners understand the nuances of AI adoption in HRM, with an emphasis on the importance of inclusive methods and ethical frameworks.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: The Role of Digital Tourism Platforms in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals in the Industry 4.0 Era
hot.abstract: The intersection of digitalization and sustainability is reshaping the tourism industry, with digital platforms playing a transformative role in optimizing travel experiences while simultaneously influencing economic inclusivity, labor dynamics, and environmental responsibility. This paper explores how Industry 4.0 technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT)—are integrated into digital tourism platforms, assessing their dual impact on sustainability and market structures. The study develops a conceptual framework around five key dimensions: market power and digital dependency, AI-driven automation and workforce transformation, innovation and digital inclusion, sustainability innovations, and data security and governance. While digital platforms enhance personalization, operational efficiency, and eco-conscious travel, they also reinforce economic disparities, monopolization, and regulatory challenges, raising concerns related to SDGs such as SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption, and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The study highlights the need for equitable governance frameworks to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven monopolization, algorithmic bias, and data privacy violations while ensuring digital accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on platform economics, digital governance, and sustainable tourism transformation, offering policy and managerial implications for fostering an inclusive and envi

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In today's business environment, green or sustainable claims are rising as companies strive to strengthen environmental practices in response to climate change and sustainable development challenges. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure to adopt more efficient sustainable practices, which may lead some to exploit sustainability efforts for their own gain. Many companies make environmentally friendly assertions to conceal or mask their actual activities—a phenomenon known as greenwashing—which fosters public scepticism about the authenticity of their green messaging. This study employs an event study methodology to examine how the stock market values greenwashing news, drawing on 121 global greenwashing news since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal a negative correlation between greenwashing news and stock market reactions. The market reactions to greenwashing news are more negative for firms with greater ESG performance than for weak ESG performance. Additionally, greenwashing news supported by concrete evidence elicits stronger adverse reactions. Companies operating in the manufacturing industry experience more significant market value losses than those in the service sector. The findings also indicate that the Asia-Pacific market demonstrates particularly strong negative responses to greenwashing news compared to other stock markets. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainability practices by providing empirical insights in a global context.

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: Effective Advertising and its Influence on Consumer Buying Behavior
hot.abstract: Advertising is a way of communication to convince an audience for taking purchase decision about a product or service and delivering information to viewers. This paper examines the relationship between environmental response and emotional response which are independent variables with dependent variable i.e. consumer buying behavior. This research investigates the relationship between the variables involved, by taking the 200 responses in twins’ cities of Pakistan. Findings of this study show the moderate relationship between independent variables and dependent variable. It shows that consumer purchase those brands from which they are emotionally attached. This study reports new results in the field of buying behavior of consumers’ response.

latest.title: A bibliometric and content analysis of marketing in Web 3.0
latest.abstract: The transition to Web 3.0 driven by blockchain, non-fungible tokens (NFTs), and the metaverse presents a transformative paradigm shift for digital marketing. Yet, the current body of academic research remains notably fragmented. This study systematically maps the intellectual structure of Web 3.0 marketing to consolidate existing knowledge, uncover dominant trends, and propose a cohesive agenda for future research. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a comprehensive bibliometric and content analysis of 121 documents from the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection spanning 2009 to 2025. Leveraging analytical tools including Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CitNetExplorer, the study maps citation networks, keyword co-occurrences, and bibliographic coupling. The findings demonstrate an exponential surge in academic interest starting in 2021 and reveal three distinct thematic clusters: (1) blockchain’s foundational role in marketing operations and advertising systems; (2) ethical considerations, trust-building, and decentralized consumer relationship management; and (3) immersive consumer engagement through the metaverse and digital technologies. The research also synthesizes the key theoretical frameworks driving the field, specifically the Theory of Planned Behavior, Social Exchange Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Value Co-creation Theory. By identifying critical gaps such as cross-platform behavioral dynamics, the long-term sustainability of gamified loyalty, and equitable stakeholder governance, this paper establishes a conceptual framework designed to guide both scholarly investigation and managerial implementation in the decentralized digital economy.

latest.title: Coping with sustainability information overload: The role of generative artificial intelligence literacy
latest.venue: Ho Chi Minh City Open University Journal of Science- Economics and Business Administration
latest.abstract: Consumers can use sustainability information to consume responsibly; however, excessive and complex sustainability claims might confuse consumers and hinder proper evaluations. Based on cognitive appraisal theory, this study empirically investigates the impacts of sustainability information overload (SIO) on green information avoidance (GIA) and green information verification behavior (GIVB) and examines the moderating role of generative AI literacy (GAIL) and the associations of GIA and GIVB with green purchase decision confidence (GPDC). Data from an online cross-sectional survey of 468 adult consumers in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings revealed that SIO positively influenced GIA, and GIA negatively influenced GPDC. However, SIO did not negatively influence GIVB on average. GAIL significantly moderated the SIO-GIVB relationship: SIO was negatively associated with GIVB at low GAIL but not significantly at mean or high GAIL.GIVB positively influenced GPDC. An indirect effect of SIO on GPDC through GIA is significant, but the indirect effect through GIVB is not significant unconditionally. These results suggest that sustainability information overload is associated with distinct coping responses. From a practical perspective, sustainability portals and shopping applications involving GenAI should emphasize evaluability and verifiability rather than enhancing disclosures. Through defining GAIL as a digitally mediated capability from the consumer’s perspective which can serve as a coping tool, this paper builds on cognitive appraisal theory in the context of AI-mediated sustainable consumption and explains the critical engagement of consumers with sustainability information amid overload situations

latest.title: The impact of environmental knowledge on water waste in restaurants on complaining behavior intention: The mediating role of perceived motivation and skepticism
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of environmental knowledge about water waste in restaurants on consumers' intentions to complain, while also elucidating the mediating roles of perceived motivation and skepticism in this relationship. A scenario-based experimental research design was employed, and data were gathered from 388 restaurant goers through an online survey. Participants were randomly assigned to two restaurant scenarios: one in which water-saving practices were not observable and another in which they were prominently displayed. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analyses in SPSS 26 and AMOS 23. The research findings demonstrate that, in the first scenario—characterized by the absence of visible communication about water conservation—environmental knowledge had no direct, significant influence on the intention to display complaint behavior. Environmental knowledge increased perceived motivation and skepticism. Perceived motivation did not directly and significantly influence the intention to engage in complaint behavior; however, skepticism increased the intention to engage in such behavior. In the second scenario, where water-saving methods were visible, environmental knowledge directly and positively affected the intention to complain, perceived motivation, and skepticism; furthermore, perceived motivation and skepticism partially mediated the relationship between environmental knowledge and the intention to complain. The findings suggest that restaurants must not only implement eco-friendly practices but also communicate them to consumers in a transparent, visible, and trustworthy way. In this context, restaurant managers should create informative visuals and communication strategies that promote water

latest.title: From sustainability practices to consumer behaviour: a PLS-SEM analysis of sustainable packaging adoption in the FMCG food sector
latest.abstract: Growing environmental concerns and plastic waste are driving the need for sustainable packaging solutions for the FMCG food sector. Understanding consumer attitude and purchasing behavior for sustainably packaged food products is crucial for promoting sustainable practices. This study assesses the association between the 5R's sustainability practices, consumer attitude, purchase intention, and actual purchasing behavior towards sustainably packaged FMCG food products. Primary data were collected from 210 consumers using the purposive sampling method from various hypermarkets in Coimbatore city. The data were analysed by Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling with SmartPLS 4 software. From the results, it is revealed that 5R sustainability practices significantly influence consumer attitude (β = 0.730) towards sustainably packaged food products. Furthermore, consumer attitude has a positive influence on purchase intention (β = 0.666), whereas purchase intention considerably influences actual purchasing behavior (β = 0.543). However, the direct association between attitude and actual purchasing behavior was not significant (β = −0.115), indicating the existence of an intention–behavior gap in sustainable consumption. The structural model explains 53.3% of the variance in attitude, 44.4% in purchase intention, and 22.5% in actual purchasing behavior, highlighting that purchase intention acts as a key mediating factor between attitude and actual behavior. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening consumer intention and improving the availability of sustainably packaged food products to enhance actual purchasing behaviour

latest.title: Cosmopolitismo del consumidor y disposición a pagar por sostenibilidad en consumidores hondureños: estudio transversal
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Objective: To analyze the relationship between consumer cosmopolitanism and willingness to pay for sustainability in global supply chains among Honduran consumers. Method: Quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study. After screening 354 responses to an online questionnaire, the analytic sample comprised 284 adults living in Honduras (63.7% women; age M = 34.41, SD = 10.41). A three-dimensional cosmopolitanism measure based on the C-COSMO scale and a measure of willingness to pay for fair labor conditions and environmental care based on willingness to pay for fair trade were administered. Confirmatory factor analyses and a structural equation model with second-order factors and robust estimation were conducted. Results: The measures showed high internal consistency (ω = .902–.957) and AVE above .50, although two cosmopolitanism dimensions showed insufficient discriminant validity (HTMT = .948). The structural model showed acceptable fit (CFI = .949; RMSEA = .079; SRMR = .043). Cosmopolitanism was positively associated with willingness to pay for sustainability (β = .64, 95% CI [.50, .78], p < .001) and explained 41% of its variance. Conclusions: More cosmopolitan consumers report greater willingness to pay for imported products made under fair labor conditions and with environmental care. The cross-sectional design, convenience sampling, and common method variance limit generalization and causal inference. Keywords: consumer cosmopolitanism, willingness to pay, sustainable consumption, global supply chains, Honduras Resumen Objetivo: Analizar la relación entre el cosmopolitismo del consumidor y la disposición a pagar por sostenibilidad en cadenas de suministro globales en consumidores hondureños. Método: Estudio cuantitativo, no experimental y transversal. Tras

latest.title: Making reusable packaging infrastructures: consumption work in the circular economy
latest.abstract: This article investigates the consumption work involved in developing workplace reuse infrastructures to support more sustainable consumption practices. Reusable food and beverage packaging systems invite a radically different mode of consumption to the throwaway culture of disposable food and beverage packaging. But making the shift from single-use to reuse presents a range of creative provocations for research on workplace sustainable consumption and circular economy transitions. What kinds of socio-technical, material and economic infrastructures are needed to support reuse, and what is the role of consumers in designing and animating those infrastructures? These issues are investigated through a case study of Australian start-up Returnr, a business developing reusable packaging systems for various contexts. The focus is on Returnr Workplace Micropool – an initiative which offers sets of reusable food and beverage containers to workplaces to reduce single-use packaging consumption. By bringing an ‘infrastructural perspective’ on sustainable consumption into conversation with the sociological notion of ‘consumption work’, the analysis brings to light some of the hidden work done by consumers in constructing, animating and resisting the infrastructures that enable workplace reusable packaging systems, an under-researched area. Following Science and Technology Studies scholarship on infrastructure, the approach developed resists a tendency to read infrastructure as a simple backdrop against which activities take place. The research demonstrates that workplace infrastructures perform a range of functions that limit, enable and could potentially obligate more sustainable consumption practices, but the agency and labour of consumers in this process needs more intentional c

latest.title: Examining the relationship between lifestyle and sustainable consumption behavior
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between different lifestyle preferences among young consumers and the sub-dimensions of sustainable consumption behavior. Lifestyle was examined through three dimensions as healthy eating and awareness, positivity, and communication while sustainable consumption behavior was addressed through environmental awareness, non-essential purchasing, saving, and reusability. Data for the study were collected from 643 participants via convenience sampling method using a questionnaire. SPSS and Smart PLS programs were used to analyze the data, and Structural Equation Modeling was applied to test the hypotheses developed in the study. The findings indicate that increases in the dimensions of healthy lifestyle and awareness positively affect the dimensions of sustainable consumption behavior such as environmental sensitivity, saving, and reusability; however, they have no significant effect on non-essential purchasing behavior. In contrast, the effects of the positivity and communication dimensions of lifestyle on sustainable consumption behavior are limited; in particular, their relationships with non-essential purchasing and environmental awareness were not found to be statistically significant.

latest.title: Green Human Resource Management and Environmental Performance in Tanzanian Local Government Authorities: The Role of Green Organizational Culture and Organizational Citizenship Behaviour towards Environment
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: This study investigated the effect of Green Human Resource Management on Environmental Performance in Tanzanian Local Government Authorities (LGAs) with a focus on the mediating effect of Green Organisational Culture and the moderating effect of Organisational Citizenship Behaviour toward Environment.A quantitative research design was adopted, and the study was conducted among employees of Tanzanian LGAs.Respondents were selected using stratified and simple random sampling techniques.A total of 400 questionnaires were given out, 231(57.8%) of which were completed and used for analysis.Data were analysed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), using Smart-PLS 4. Findings showed that Green Human Resource Management had a positive effect on Environmental Performance.Furthermore, the findings show that the relationship between Green Human Resource Management and Environmental Performance is positively and significantly mediated by Green Organisational Culture.This implies that a green organisational culture enhances the effect of Green Human Resource Management on environmental performance.The findings also showed that Organisational Citizenship Behaviour toward Environment positively and significantly moderates the relationship between Green Human Resource Management and Environmental Performance, meaning that the positive effect of Green Human Resource Management on environmental performance is stronger when employees engage in higher levels of voluntary environmental behaviour.The study recommends LGAs to improve Green Human Resource Management functions for better environmental performance.LGAs should also improve green organisational culture and promote environmental citizenship behaviour of employees to maximise the environmental benefits a

latest.title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

latest.title: From Triple Bottom Line (TBL) to Supply Chain Triple Value Bottom Line (SCTVBL): A Sustainable Supply Chain Value Framework
latest.abstract: In today's competitive business environment where consumers increasingly expect transparency, quality, and value for money, buying a product means interacting with the entire supply chain. As the modern supply chains become more autonomous and interconnected, the effective measurement of their business value necessitates transitioning from the conventional efficiency‐based business models to more holistic, stakeholder‐focused business models. In this regard, although the triple bottom line (TBL) framework offers sustainability of the supply chains via economic, social, and environmental performance dimensions, it does not segregate and comprehensively capture value for the key supply chain stakeholders, thereby disregarding the important stakeholders like employees, customers, suppliers, and partners. Therefore, by evaluating the gaps in the extant supply chain management literature coupled with analyzing, critiquing, and synthesizing the current supply chain performance frameworks, and drawing upon the guiding theories, this research introduces a novel concept, “supply chain triple value bottom line” (SCTVBL), and subsequently presents a SCTVBL framework. While addressing the evolving performance needs of the contemporary supply chains, the proposed framework further extends the conventional TBL framework by offering value‐oriented supply chains perspective. As a whole, by suggesting organizational value creation (via economic value, operational value, and employee value), socio‐environmental value creation (via social value and environmental value), and relational value creation (via customer value and supplier & partner value) as renewed supply chain value dimensions, the SCTVBL framework offers a more stakeholder‐focused perspective for holistically addressing the v

latest.title: Beyond resistance: deinfluencing, consumer activism and the incorporation of critique on digital platforms
latest.abstract: Deinfluencing is a social media trend where content creators advise audiences not to buy ‘must-have,’ overhyped, overpriced, low-quality, or unnecessary products. It serves as a potential form of resistance to the logic of overconsumption. Gaining momentum on TikTok in early 2023, deinfluencing rapidly spread across social media platforms where the meanings and norms of consumption are publicly negotiated and can acquire collective relevance. This conceptual paper proposes a critical reading of the phenomenon, arguing that deinfluencing does not necessarily constitute a negation of influencer marketing, but may instead be incorporated into the commercial arrangements it contests while retaining critical meanings and effects. Situated at the intersection of consumer culture, consumer activism, influencer marketing and platformisation, the paper examines the infrastructural and commercial conditions through which consumer critique acquires visibility and value. It develops a multilevel conceptual model comprising three analytically distinct but potentially overlapping mechanisms through which critical discourse can be incorporated into influencer marketing: substitution , at the content level, whereby criticism of particular products redirects rather than rejects consumption; hybridisation , at the level of practices, whereby influencing and deinfluencing coexist within creators’ communicative repertoire; and authenticity renewal , at the level of audience relations, whereby rejecting some products can strengthen creator credibility and, under certain conditions, the persuasive value of subsequent endorsements. Platformisation conditions the circulation and visibility of these critical practices without determining their effects. Drawing on the sociological concept of bou

latest.title: Paradoxical leadership and preschool teachers' innovative behavior: the mediating role of psychological capital and the moderating role of professional identity
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examined how kindergarten-level paradoxical leadership, characterized by high performance expectations and strong management support, is associated with preschool teachers' innovative behavior, and whether psychological capital and professional identity explain and condition this association. Methods Survey data from 1,029 preschool teachers nested within 91 kindergartens in China were analyzed using multilevel models to account for the hierarchical data structure. Indirect and conditional indirect associations were evaluated using cluster bootstrap confidence intervals obtained by resampling kindergartens. Results The findings showed that paradoxical leadership was positively associated with teachers' psychological capital and innovative behavior. Psychological capital accounted for a positive indirect association between paradoxical leadership and innovative behavior at the between-kindergarten level. Professional identity strengthened the positive association between paradoxical leadership and psychological capital, as well as the corresponding indirect association with innovative behavior. At lower levels of professional identity, neither association was statistically distinguishable from zero. Discussion These findings suggest that paradoxical leadership is associated with preschool teachers' innovative behavior partly through their psychological capital, with professional identity shaping the strength of this pathway. By identifying a cross-level psychological pathway and its boundary condition, the study extends paradoxical leadership research to early childhood education. latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Mechanisms of Sustainability Influencer Communication: Credibility, Green Trust, and Greenwashing
latest.abstract: The aim of this study is to explore the communication mechanisms through which social media influencers can influence consumers’ environmentally conscious attitudes and their intention to make sustainable purchases. According to the literature, the credibility of the source, value alignment, self-congruity, and parasocial relationships play a key role in the effectiveness of influencer communication. According to a synthesis of the literature, green trust can act as a mediating mechanism contributing to the development of sustainable purchasing intentions, while the perception of greenwashing can weaken the effects of credibility and trust. Even influencers who do not directly address sustainability can have a positive impact if their communication is consistent and aligned with their followers’ values. The theoretical contribution of this study is the development of an integrated conceptual model.

latest.title: What drives sustainable fashion behaviour: fashion interest and environmental attitudes
latest.abstract: Introduction: The fashion industry is among the most resource-intensive and polluting consumer sectors, and consumer behavior is central to reducing its environmental impact. Although research has extensively examined pro-environmental attitudes, it has treated fashion interest inconsistently, often assuming it conflicts with sustainability despite evidence that sustainable consumers can be highly fashion-conscious. This study examines how environmental attitudes and fashion interest relate to clothing behavior across the consumption cycle, distinguishing three behavioral types: sufficiency (buying less, keeping garments longer), care and efficiency (maintenance, repair, lower-impact laundering), and circular and reuse (second-hand acquisition and diverting used clothing from disposal). Materials and methods: Drawing on an online survey of 2000 Canadian consumers, we measured fashion interest using standardized scales. We regressed each of 27 ordinal outcomes on the two attitudes using ordered logistic regression; reported odds ratios per standard deviation, with and without demographic controls; and verified results with Brant tests, generalized ordered logit models, and false-discovery-rate correction. Results: The two attitudes function as distinct motivational orientations, with associations that vary systematically by behavioral type. Environmental attitude is positively associated with sustainable behavior across all three types and is unaffected by demographic controls. Fashion interest is the strongest predictor of purchase frequency but is not uniformly unsustainable: it is positively associated with circular and reuse behaviors, negatively with sufficiency behaviors, and only weakly and inconsistently with care and efficiency behaviors. latest.title: Sostenibilidad rentable o gasto empresarial: evaluación del valor económico de las prácticas responsables en pequeños hoteles del contexto de la Ciudad de Esmeraldas
latest.abstract: La sostenibilidad plantea una decisión compleja para los pequeños hoteles: comprometer recursos limitados en medidas cuyos beneficios pueden aparecer en distintos plazos y dimensiones. Este artículo propone una matriz costo–beneficio para evaluar prácticas responsables en pequeños hoteles de la ciudad de Esmeraldas sin presuponer su rentabilidad. Se desarrolló una revisión narrativa dirigida de 22 fuentes bibliográficas y técnicas, complementada con un modelo de flujos incrementales y cinco escenarios hipotéticos de energía, agua, desperdicio alimentario y capacitación. La evaluación distingue inversión inicial, costos recurrentes, ahorro bruto, valor actual neto, relación beneficio–costo y recuperación; los efectos sociales y ambientales se registran mediante indicadores independientes. Con una tasa real supuesta del 10 %, tres escenarios presentan valor actual neto positivo, mientras el fotovoltaico registra −939,78 USD en diez años, aunque su recuperación simple es de 6,67 años. La reducción del ahorro bruto en 25 % mantiene negativos los escenarios de capacitación y fotovoltaica. Estos resultados son demostrativos y no representan mediciones de hoteles de Esmeraldas. La contribución consiste en un procedimiento transparente para identificar condiciones de viabilidad, evitar doble contabilización y comparar decisiones de inversión con beneficios no monetizados. Su aplicación empírica requiere registros de consumo y ocupación, cotizaciones, medición de resultados y validación contextual.

latest.title: Greenwashing skepticism as a selective moderator: how digital environmental content exposure shapes green e-commerce intentions among Saudi university students
latest.abstract: Introduction As Generation Z consumers increasingly engage with digital platforms in response to environmental considerations, understanding how online sustainability messaging shapes green e-commerce behavior becomes more pressing. Digitalization is often assumed to equalize access to sustainability information, yet digital divide research shows that inequalities persist in how online content is converted into outcomes. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study examines how exposure to digital environmental content (DECE) shapes green e-consumption intention (GECI) among digitally literate Saudi university students. Methods Environmental awareness and personal responsibility (EAR) and message credibility (MC) were modeled as two parallel mediators linking DECE to GECI, with no hypothesized path between them. Greenwashing perception (GP) was expected to moderate specifically the effect of MC on GECI, and perceived barriers (PB) were examined as an independent predictor of GECI. Data from 305 respondents were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results The model explained substantial variance in GECI ( R ² = 0.603; Q ² = 0.577). DECE had a significant direct effect on GECI ( β = 0.190, p = 0.001). The EAR-mediated pathway was dominant ( β = 0.311, f ² = 0.333), whereas the MC-mediated pathway was non-significant ( β = 0.006, p = 0.823). GP moderated the credibility–intention link (MC → GECI; β = −0.114, p = 0.005) but not the exposure–intention link (DECE → GECI; β = 0.070, p = 0.095), suggesting that greenwashing skepticism acts as a credibility-related barrier. PB was positively associated with GECI ( β = 0.138, p = 0.023), a counter-intuitive association interpreted tentativ

latest.title: Necro-Branding in ethical fashion: the moderating roles of minimalist visuals and celebrity characteristics with the mediating role of moral resonance
latest.abstract: This study explores Necro-Branding, the use of deceased celebrities in marketing, as a novel strategy to boost consumer engagement in ethical fashion on social media. Analysing 12,518 Instagram posts from 11 ethical fashion accounts using tools including Google Cloud Vision and the Moral Foundations Dictionary, we find Necro-Celebrity endorsements significantly enhance engagement. The effect is moderated by minimalist visuals and celebrity traits, mediated by moral resonance. More visible and older celebrities perform best. Our research provides the first empirical evidence on the role of Necro-Branding in ethical fashion, with the causal main effect and the mediating role of moral resonance confirmed in a follow-up online experiment. These findings provide strategic guidance for marketers seeking to promote sustainability while respectfully leveraging legacy figures for strong(er) audience connection.

latest.title: Impact of Sustainability-Oriented Marketing on Consumer Attitudes and Purchase Decisions
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The increasing urgency of environmental and social challenges has positioned sustainability at the forefront of modern marketing practices. This study explores the role of marketing and consumer behavior in achieving a sustainable future by examining how marketing strategies influence consumer attitudes and purchasing decisions toward environmentally responsible products. The research focuses on key elements such as green advertising, eco-labeling, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives, and their impact on shaping consumer perceptions and trust. Using a combination of primary and secondary data, the study analyzes consumer awareness, preferences, and behavioral patterns related to sustainable consumption. The findings indicate a significant positive relationship between sustainability-oriented marketing efforts and pro-environmental consumer behavior. Consumers are increasingly inclined to support brands that demonstrate transparency, ethical practices, and environmental commitment, although factors such as price sensitivity and limited awareness continue to affect purchasing decisions. The study highlights the importance of leveraging consumer insights to design effective marketing strategies that encourage responsible consumption. It concludes that businesses integrating sustainability into their marketing frameworks can enhance brand loyalty, gain competitive advantage, and contribute meaningfully to sustainable development. The research offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers, and organizations aiming to foster a more sustainable and consumer-driven marketplace.

latest.title: Buy Smart: Estudio piloto de un juego de mesa cooperativo para trabajar el consumo responsable en educación infantil
latest.abstract: This study presents a pilot assessment of the effectiveness and potential for improvement of a cooperative board game aimed at promoting the purchase of local and seasonal products and reducing waste generation. The game was piloted in three preschool classrooms comprising 41 children aged 4-5 years. Qualitative feedback was collected from teachers to assess its playability, suitability, and pedagogical value. Educators highlighted the importance of engaging materials, simple rules, and prior contextual instruction to support meaningful participation. The findings suggest that, although responsible consumption is a challenging concept for children at this developmental stage, sustainability learning can be supported by collaborative games through guided play. Finally, the study provides a framework for evaluating analogue educational games and underscores the potential of play-based learning to promote critical environmental thinking in early childhood education.

latest.title: Green Organizational Culture, Green Innovation, and Environmental Performance: A Bibliometric Analysis
latest.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
latest.abstract: Green Organizational Culture (GOC) plays an important role in shaping environmentally friendly behavior within organizations, although previous research has reported mixed findings regarding its influence on performance. This study aims to describe the development of GOC research from 2021 to 2026 using a bibliometric approach. Data were collected from Google Scholar through Publish or Perish, resulting in 200 documents that were analyzed using VOSviewer. The analysis examined publication trends, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, thematic development, and research opportunities. The results indicate a substantial increase in GOC publications during the last two years, particularly in 2025 and 2026. The keyword co-occurrence analysis reveals five thematic clusters covering green innovation, organizational culture and employee behavior, leadership and performance, sustainability, and green human resource management (GHRM). Organizational culture emerges as a central theme connecting these research areas. The findings also identify several topics, including green competency, green organizational citizenship, job satisfaction, and employee green behavior, that remain relatively underexplored in relation to green culture. These findings provide an overview of research trends and potential directions for future studies while helping practitioners understand the development of GOC research and its connections with environmental sustainability and organizational performance.

latest.title: Exploring the Key Drivers of Online Purchasing Behaviour for Organic Food Products
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: The growing consumption of organic food products, coupled with the rapid expansion of digital commerce, has significantly transformed consumer purchasing behaviour. The present study examines the key factors influencing consumers’ online purchasing behaviour towards organic food products, based on primary data collected from 200 respondents in Hyderabad city. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire designed to assess consumer perceptions across the pre-purchase, purchase, post-purchase, and other influencing dimensions. Descriptive statistics and Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) were employed to analyse the data and identify the major determinants of online purchasing behaviour. The findings indicate that time efficiency in obtaining product information is the most important consideration during the pre-purchase stage, while delivery time is the leading determinant during the purchase stage. In the post-purchase phase, customer service support emerges as a crucial factor influencing consumer satisfaction and retention. The Exploratory Factor Analysis identifies five underlying dimensions: timeliness, price and certification, trustworthiness, serviceability and innovativeness. Together, these factors explain 64.04% of the total variance, highlighting their importance in shaping consumers’ online purchasing decisions. The findings offer valuable insights for online retailers and organic food marketers in developing customer-oriented marketing strategies.

latest.title: Marketing’s Role in Building Conscious Consumerism
latest.venue: Jharkhand Journal of Development and Management Studies
latest.abstract: For many decades now, sustainability has been on the agenda of academia and policy. But sustainability is a perennial theme for several reasons. One issue arises from the inconsistency between belief and practice, that is, consumers believe in positive social values but do not necessarily always act accordingly. This paper reflects on the research results and empirical observations related to the role of marketing in promoting conscious consumerism by shaping an individual’s positive attitudes andbehavior. The paper suggests propositions by integrating the Norms Activation Model, Theory of Planned Behavior; signaling theory, trust, and brand equity. This paper presents research findings concerning the influence of awareness and perceived importance on the implementation of sustainability principles in community-based tourism development in Indonesia. The objective of presenting these diverse perspectives is to gain an understanding of the various factors that can constitute conscious consumption grounded in sustainability values.

latest.title: An Integrative Explanation Framework for the IntentionBehavior Gap in Green Consumption: Based on SOR Theory
latest.venue: Academic journal of management and social sciences
latest.abstract: Against the backdrop of global dualcarbon goals and sustainable development strategies, green consumption has become a critical pathway to reduce resource waste, protect ecological environment, and promote the comprehensive green transformation of economy and society. However, the widespread intentionbehavior gap, namely "words over deeds", has become a prominent bottleneck restricting the popularization of green consumption. Existing studies have scattered identification of influencing factors, and lack a systematic integrative framework as well as a precise matching mechanism between causes and interventions. Based on the StimulusOrganismResponse (SOR) theory, this paper constructs an integrative explanation framework through systematic literature analysis. The results show that the intentionbehavior gap is jointly driven by external stimuli (product factors and environmental factors) and internal organismic factors (attitude, motivation, behavioral habit, and environmental sentiment). Correspondingly, three targeted intervention strategies are proposed: anthropomorphism, ecolabeling, and nudging. This study provides a unified analytical perspective for explaining the green consumption intentionbehavior gap, and offers actionable decision references for enterprises and government authorities.

latest.title: Young consumers’ behavioral intentions toward farm-to-table restaurants in a Muslim-majority market: motivations, emotions and well-being perceptions
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how the theory of consumption values (TCV), consumption motivations and emotions influence young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which subsequently shape brand love, brand respect and behavioral intentions toward halal farm-to-table (FTT) restaurants. It also compared same-ethnic and cross-ethnic Generation Z consumers to examine whether cultural background moderates the proposed relationships within this restaurant context. Design/methodology/approach This study used a quantitative research design by collecting data from 420 Generation Z consumers who had recently dined at halal FTT restaurants serving ethnic cuisine. Data were collected through on-site surveys at selected restaurant locations to ensure that respondents had a direct and recent dining experience for the study’s context. The data were subsequently analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Economic value, consumption motivations and emotions were found to significantly enhance young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which in turn positively influenced brand love and brand respect. Importantly, well-being perception significantly influenced behavioral intentions indirectly through both brand love and brand respect, highlighting these brand-related mechanisms as important pathways linking well-being perceptions to behavioral intentions toward halal FTT restaurants. Both brand love and brand respect significantly strengthened behavioral intentions toward halal FTT restaurants. Multi-group analysis further showed that cultural background did not significantly moderate these relationships, indicating that the effects of brand love and brand respect on behavioral intentions were consistent across same-ethnic and cross-ethnic Generation Z c

latest.title: Formation of green purchase behavior among Indonesian Generation Z consumers: extending norm activation theory with green price sensitivity
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine why environmental awareness among Indonesian Generation Z consumers does not consistently translate into green purchase behavior (GPB) by testing the roles of awareness of consequences (AC), ascription of responsibility (AR), personal norms (PN) and green price sensitivity (GPS) within norm activation theory (NAT). Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 342 Indonesian Generation Z consumers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test direct, mediating and moderated mediation effects.
