To achieve this goal, 47 interviews were conducted with practitioners from local authorities to identify the key elements that facilitate or hinder the implementation of CE. The findings highlight the crucial role of local authorities in enabling the transition to a CE, with critical support from political endorsement, strategic foresight, and effective leadership. However, obstacles such as organizational inertia, financial constraints, and a limited understanding of a CE present challenges to a CE's broader adoption. The study also emphasizes the critical role of partnerships and collaborative networks in overcoming these barriers and promoting the advancement of CE initiatives.

hot.title: Product reuse and repurpose in circular manufacturing: a critical review of key challenges, shortcomings and future directions
hot.abstract: This paper explores the transformative potential of reuse and repurposing strategies in the manufacturing industry, with a focus on sustainability and circular economy principles. Through an extensive review of 115 articles from Scopus using 6 different queries for broad topic coverage, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of reuse and repurposing frameworks, highlighting their benefits and challenges. The research identifies three essential pillars for successful implementation: product design, operational processes, and consumer acceptance. The study emphasizes the significance of modular designs, lifecycle extensions, and advanced cost models to maximize resource efficiency and sustainability. The paper also discusses the integration of advanced technologies, such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and IoT-enabled systems, to enhance traceability, streamline reverse logistics, and optimize predictive maintenance. Automated disassembly and collaborative robotics are highlighted as critical enablers for efficient and scalable reuse operations. Furthermore, the study advocates for flexible supply chains and real-time data analytics to address uncertainties in core acquisition and product variability. Despite the progress, the lack of standardized frameworks and metrics remains a significant barrier to widespread adoption. The paper concludes by proposing a cohesive framework that incorporates technological advancements, regulatory support, and collaborative approaches to overcome these limitations. This study provides actionable insights to foster a scalable, transparent, and sustainable manufacturing ecosystem.

hot.title: Digital marketing strategies in expanding the market for MSME creative products in Indonesia—state of art
hot.abstract: Digital marketing strategy is the planning and actions taken by companies or individuals to utilize digital technology to market products or services effectively and efficiently to target markets. In this strategy, companies use various digital channels such as social media, search engines, email marketing, websites, or e-commerce to achieve marketing objectives, including increasing brand awareness, attracting new customers, and boosting sales and customer loyalty. However, challenges in using digital marketing still exist due to the digital literacy gap among creative product practitioners. This study reviews digital marketing for creative products, including social media marketing, search engine marketing, influencer marketing, email marketing, and content marketing. Using Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) method, 22 articles from leading sources such as MDPI, Wiley, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore were analyzed. The objectives of this study are to determine (1) what the definitions of digital marketing strategies and the creative product market are. (2) Which countries have implemented digital marketing in the creative market for SMEs? (3) Who is involved, and how familiar are SMEs with the creative product market? (4) What strategies are used in digital marketing in Indonesia? How is it implemented, what are the challenges, and what is the level of success? (R5): What are the future research and recommendations for digital marketing in expanding the creative market? Future research directions include the application of AI and technology for automated content creation for creative product practitioners, strengthened digital education and literacy, and community-based campaigns that foster collaboration among local creators to build a mutually supportive e

hot.title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Factors for Sustainable Tourism Development: The Way Forward Toward Destination Resilience and Growth
hot.abstract: Although environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance is increasingly gaining popularity in corporate and financial domains, its application in the tourism industry is still relatively underexplored. Hence, the objectives of this research are fivefold: (1) A systematic review appraises the extant literature on the intersection of the ESG dimensions and sustainable tourism; (2) It provides a synthesis of the content of the extracted articles and maps thematic intersections related to travel destinations' environmental stewardship, social equity and governance frameworks; (3) It assesses ESG‐aligned strategies that are intended to address the destinations' challenges including their carrying capacities and overtourism issues, climate risks, sociocultural tensions as well as institutional accountabilities; (4) It provides a holistic conceptual framework that guides policymakers, practitioners and stakeholders in integrating ESG into tourism planning and development, for sustainable and economically viable outcomes. In conclusion, (5) it advances theoretical and managerial implications.

hot.title: Green human resources management and green innovation: a meta-analytic review of strategic human resources levers for environmental sustainability
hot.abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has become a vital lever for driving organizational sustainability, yet the empirical relationship between GHRM and Green Innovation (GI) remains fragmented and inconclusive. This meta-analysis integrates findings from 52 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025, encompassing 23,103 observations, to estimate the overall effect of GHRM on GI and to examine the influence of specific HR practices and contextual moderators. Grounded in the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, the Resource-Based View (RBV), and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study reveals a significant positive pooled effect, affirming that GHRM is a consistent and influential driver of GI. Among HR practices, green-linked compensation demonstrated the strongest impact, surpassing training and recruitment. Moderator analyses reveal that effect sizes differ meaningfully by industry type, firm size, and year of publication, but not by country development status or statistical method. These results contribute to theoretical advancement by integrating behavioral, strategic, and cognitive perspectives on sustainability-oriented innovation. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for managers and policymakers on designing effective GHRM systems that stimulate eco-innovation. This study delivers the first quantitative synthesis clarifying when, where, and how GHRM enhances green innovation across diverse sectors and economies, providing a robust foundation for future research and strategy in sustainability-driven human capital development.

hot.title: The implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation for sustainability
hot.abstract: The interconnected phenomena of digital transformation and environmental innovation exert a major impact on sustainability . This research attempts to shed light on the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation. Both digital transformation and environmental innovation offer multiple opportunities to address global challenges such as climate change , resource depletion , and social inequality. This study highlights the need to integrate digital technologies and innovation with environmental initiatives. By following this approach, the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation can lead to a more resilient and sustainable society. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is used to determine the necessary or sufficient factors to increase sustainability. The study thus provides insights into what the environmental priorities should be. The results show how to reduce environmental impacts , improve quality of life , and support economic development. They can also be used to inform policies that support sustainability initiatives by encouraging the combinations of interventions that work best. By harnessing the potential of digital transformation and environmental innovation, it is possible to build a greener and more prosperous future for generations to come.

hot.title: Toward a Resilient and Sustainable Supply Chain: Operational Responses to Global Disruptions in the Post-COVID-19 Era
hot.abstract: Global supply chains have faced unprecedented disruptions in recent years, ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to geopolitical tensions and climate-induced shocks. These events have exposed structural vulnerabilities in operational models overly optimized for efficiency at the expense of resilience and sustainability. This conceptual paper proposes an integrated framework linking resilience enablers, post-pandemic operational strategies, and sustainability outcomes. Through a synthesis of the interdisciplinary literature across operations management, sustainability science, institutional theory, and organizational behavior, we develop typologies of operational responses—including agile, lean–green, circular, and decentralized models—and connect them to broader Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on systems thinking and the Triple Bottom Line framework, we present a conceptual model that outlines causal relationships between resilience drivers, adaptive operational strategies, and long-term sustainable performance. The paper further discusses policy implications for public and private sectors, offering insights for global sustainability governance. We conclude by outlining a research agenda to empirically test and refine the model through multi-method approaches. This study contributes to theory by reconceptualizing sustainable operations in the context of compound global disruptions and offers a normative direction for future scholarship and practice.

latest.title: Gender stereotypes and portrayals in advertising: implications for emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals in advertising shape early-stage emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults. It positions gendered advertising as both a branding issue and a responsible-marketing concern in youth-oriented marketplaces. Design/methodology/approach A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 159 valid responses from a Vietnamese sample concentrated mainly in the younger age segment; 83.6% of respondents were aged 14–26. Skincare and automobile advertising stimuli were used to manipulate stereotype congruity and the gender of the focal protagonist. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed relationships. Findings Both gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals significantly influence emotional brand attachment across the experimental conditions. Emotional brand attachment, in turn, positively predicts brand sacredness and its three dimensions: communitas, supremacy and mesmerization. The findings are interpreted as immediate relational and symbolic responses within a youth- and young-adult-oriented sample, not as evidence of fully matured brand attachment or sacredness. Originality/value This study contributes to young-consumer and gender-in-advertising research by extending attention from proximal persuasion outcomes to early relational and symbolic brand outcomes. It clarifies the conceptual distinction between gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals and explains how these cues may shape early-stage attachment and sacredness-related perceptions among young consumers and young adults. The findings also offer responsible-marketing implications: although gendered portrayals may strengthen consumer–brand

latest.title: Emotional Branding: A Comprehensive Literature Review
latest.venue: International Journal Of Applied Management And Economics
latest.abstract: Emotional branding (EB) has evolved from a practitioner-driven marketing (MKTG) philosophy mainly into a substantial stream of academic inquiry that examines how brands cultivate deep, affect-laden bonds with consumers that extend beyond functional attributes and rational appeals. This article offers a comprehensive review of the EB literature, synthesizing conceptual, theoretical, and empirical contributions published between 2005 and 2026. The review first traces the conceptual evolution of the construct, from Gobé's (2001) foundational manifesto to more recent operationalization grounded in brand attachment, brand love (BL), & brand resonance. Then, it examines the theoretical foundations that underpin this specific field, including brand relationship theory (BRT) (Fournier, 1998), attachment theory (AT), self-congruence theory (SCT), and consumer culture theory (CCT), before mapping the antecedents and outcomes of EB identified across qualitative, quantitative, and bibliometric studies. Drawing on evidence from diverse cultural and sectoral contexts, including Jordan, Indonesia, Italy, and the United States, the review demonstrates that EB consistently & positively predicts brand loyalty, brand attachment, customer satisfaction, & purchase share, while also carrying risks such as the emergence of doppelgänger brand imagery when emotional narratives are perceived as inauthentic. This review is concluded by identifying persistent gaps in the literature, particularly regarding cross-cultural generalizability, the measurement of EB as a multidimensional construct, and the paucity of longitudinal and experimental designs, and it proposes a research agenda to address these gaps. latest.title: Unlocking the nexus from innovativeness perceptions to customer loyalty: the roles of omnichannel trust and emotional brand attachment
latest.abstract: Recently, the bonding between consumers and service providers is getting more complex as the current trend shows the importance of innovation for long-run viability. Innovativeness also plays an imperative role in ensuring sustainability for hospitality businesses. Hence, the purpose of this study is to investigate the effects of a holistic concept of innovativeness on trust in omnichannel and behavioral loyalty while the mediating influences of trust in omnichannel of a restaurant and emotional brand attachment on the domain linkages were further explored. This study tested using a structured questionnaire from a sample of chain restaurant customers in Klang Valley area of Malaysia. The results indicate that menu innovativeness, technology-based service innovativeness and experiential innovativeness influence trust in omnichannel. Besides, only dimension of technology-based service innovativeness influences repeat purchase intention while experiential innovativeness influences positive electronic words of mouth (eWOM). Further findings also demonstrated that trust in omnichannel and emotional brand attachment play several important mediating roles in predicting behavioral loyalty. Through application of Stimulus-Organism-Response theory, this study assesses the impacts of innovativeness holistically that employed by restaurateurs, on trust in omnichannel of the restaurant which this perspective has never been explored previously. Apart from making theoretical contributions, this study provides additional insights on practical implications for restaurateurs to invest on salient resources accurately and to innovate their offers more effectively.

latest.title: ЗЕЛЕНИЙ МЕНЕДЖМЕНТ ЯК НАПРЯМ ІННОВАЦІЙНОГО РОЗВИТКУ ГОТЕЛЬНО-РЕСТОРАННОГО БІЗНЕСУ
latest.abstract: Досліджено теоретичні та прикладні засади впровадження зеленого менеджменту на підприємствах сфери HoReCa в Україні. Обґрунтовано доцільність обрання сфери HoReCa об’єктом дослідження через комплексне використання ресурсів та пряму взаємодію зі споживачами. Систематизовано принципи зеленого менеджменту: ресурсоефективність, превентивність, екологічну відповідальність, інноваційність та системність. На основі емпіричного дослідження (анкетування 18 підприємств HoReCa) виявлено основні бар’єри зеленої трансформації: фінансові (72%), кадрово-поведінкові (56%), інформаційні (44%), організаційні (39%). Запропоновано авторську класифікацію бар’єрів за масштабом підприємства. Розроблено інтегральний індекс зеленої трансформації підприємства (10 показників) та диференційовані заходи зеленого менеджменту для малих, середніх і великих підприємств. Доведено необхідність сприйняття зеленого менеджменту як комплексної управлінсько-інноваційної системи. Практичне значення полягає у можливості використання запропонованих заходів для планування екологічних заходів підприємствами HoReCa. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає у розробленні інтегрального індексу зеленої трансформації, удосконаленні класифікації бар’єрів на основі емпіричних даних та обґрунтуванні диференційованого механізму впровадження зеленого менеджменту залежно від масштабу підприємства.

latest.title: Beyond resistance: deinfluencing, consumer activism and the incorporation of critique on digital platforms
latest.abstract: Deinfluencing is a social media trend where content creators advise audiences not to buy ‘must-have,’ overhyped, overpriced, low-quality, or unnecessary products. It serves as a potential form of resistance to the logic of overconsumption. Gaining momentum on TikTok in early 2023, deinfluencing rapidly spread across social media platforms where the meanings and norms of consumption are publicly negotiated and can acquire collective relevance. This conceptual paper proposes a critical reading of the phenomenon, arguing that deinfluencing does not necessarily constitute a negation of influencer marketing, but may instead be incorporated into the commercial arrangements it contests while retaining critical meanings and effects. Situated at the intersection of consumer culture, consumer activism, influencer marketing and platformisation, the paper examines the infrastructural and commercial conditions through which consumer critique acquires visibility and value. It develops a multilevel conceptual model comprising three analytically distinct but potentially overlapping mechanisms through which critical discourse can be incorporated into influencer marketing: substitution , at the content level, whereby criticism of particular products redirects rather than rejects consumption; hybridisation , at the level of practices, whereby influencing and deinfluencing coexist within creators’ communicative repertoire; and authenticity renewal , at the level of audience relations, whereby rejecting some products can strengthen creator credibility and, under certain conditions, the persuasive value of subsequent endorsements. Platformisation conditions the circulation and visibility of these critical practices without determining their effects. Drawing on the sociological concept of bou

latest.title: The Role of Emotional Attachment in Mediating the Influence of Parasocial Interaction on Impulsive Buying (Study on BTS Fans in Denpasar City)
latest.abstract: The growing popularity of the Korean Wave (Hallyu) in recent years has contributed to increased consumption of South Korean popular culture products, particularly Korean pop (K-pop), across various countries, including Indonesia. The global popularity of BTS has fostered strong emotional connections between fans and their idols through digital interactions on social media platforms. These interactions may facilitate the development of parasocial relationships and emotional attachment, potentially influencing fans' consumption behavior, including impulsive buying. This study aimed to examine and explain the mediating role of emotional attachment in the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying among BTS fans, collectively known as ARMY, in Denpasar City, Indonesia. The study population comprised BTS fans residing in Denpasar City, from whom 120 respondents were selected using a nonprobability purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.0. The findings revealed that parasocial interaction had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and emotional attachment. Furthermore, emotional attachment had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and partially mediated the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying. These findings highlighted the importance of parasocial interaction and emotional attachment in explaining impulsive buying tendencies among BTS fans. The study provided insights into the psychological mechanisms underlying fan consumption behavior and offered practical implications for marketers seeking to understand consumer engagement and purchasing decisions within digital fa

latest.title: Ảnh hưởng của truyền thông mạng xã hội đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch của thế hệ Gen Z tại Việt Nam
latest.abstract: Nghiên cứu phân tích ảnh hưởng của truyền thông mạng xã hội đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch của thế hệ Gen Z tại Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp định lượng, dữ liệu được thu thập bằng khảo sát trực tuyến thông qua Google Forms đối với những người thuộc thế hệ Gen Z có sử dụng mạng xã hội để tìm kiếm, xem hoặc tương tác với nội dung về điểm đến du lịch. Sau quá trình sàng lọc và làm sạch dữ liệu, 214 phiếu hợp lệ được sử dụng để phân tích bằng phần mềm SPSS 27.0 thông qua các kỹ thuật kiểm định độ tin cậy Cronbach's alpha, phân tích nhân tố khám phá và hồi quy tuyến tính bội. Kết quả cho thấy chất lượng thông tin, nội dung do người dùng tạo ra và mức độ tương tác đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch; trong đó nội dung do người dùng tạo ra có tác động mạnh nhất. Nghiên cứu bổ sung bằng chứng thực nghiệm về vai trò của truyền thông mạng xã hội trong xây dựng thương hiệu điểm đến và đề xuất hàm ý định vị điểm đến Việt Nam theo hướng trực quan, tương tác, đáng tin cậy và phù hợp với Gen Z.

latest.title: The relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust: brand credibility, emotional attachment, and perceived quality effects
latest.abstract: Introduction The purpose of this research was to explore the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Specifically, we developed a conceptual model which proposes that brand credibility has a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust, and that perceived quality and emotional attachment have mediating effects on brand trust. Methods We tested the conceptual model by conducting a 2 × 2 (low versus high brand ethicality and low versus high brand credibility) between-subjects experiment, with brand trust as the dependent variable. Data ( N = 208) were collected at a large university in Bangladesh, and were analysed using PLS-SEM. Results Results of the experiment suggest that brand ethicality has a direct effect on brand trust. Brand ethicality also enhances emotional attachment and perceived quality, which, in turn, lead to increased brand trust. Brand credibility, however, does not have a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Discussion Drawing on signalling theory, the findings provide causal evidence that brand ethicality builds brand trust through two parallel pathways: an affective pathway via emotional attachment and a cognitive pathway via perceived quality. Contrary to expectations, brand credibility did not act as a boundary condition, suggesting that brand ethicality and brand credibility may be better understood as sequential antecedents of brand trust rather than as interacting constructs. For practice, marketers ought to increase brand ethicality to increase brand trust, both directly and via emotional attachment and perceived quality.

latest.title: How is AI companionship reshaping young consumers’ emotional engagement and future brand relationships in digital marketing?
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing by shifting engagement from transactional interactions to emotionally driven relationships. This practitioner viewpoint aims to explore the rise in AI companionship, including conversational agents, virtual influencers and emotional responsive AI systems, and their role in shaping young consumers’ engagement within digital ecosystems. These technologies enable human-like emotional interaction, fostering trust, attachment and sustained relational bonds between young consumers and AI-mediated brand environments. Design/methodology/approach This article draws on a purposive selected body of recent and seminal literature on consumer psychology to explain how parasocial interactions, anthropomorphism and emotional attachment increasingly influence young consumer-brand relationships. The literature was selected based on its relevance to the study objectives, conceptual contribution and practical implications for marketing. The reviewed studies were synthesised into connected themes, which originally provided the foundation for developing foundational practical and managerial implications presented. Findings It highlights strategic opportunities such as hyper-personalisation, continued engagement and customer value creation, while also identifying governance challenges related to transparency, emotional manipulation, data ethics and consumer vulnerability. Practical implications The viewpoint synthesises these developments into young consumers psychological transformation, strategic implications and socio-technical governance challenges. It further outlines future scenarios where AI companions become embedded actors in digital marketing ecosystems, fundamentally transforming both professional practice and soci

latest.title: Role of corporate social responsibility in brand loyalty, emotional attachment and online behavior among Generation Z consumers: a cross-national study
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the triple bottom line (TBL) framework and social identity theory (SIT), this study aims to examine how Generation Z consumers’ perceptions of the economic, environmental and social dimensions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) relate to brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, and how these relationships extend to electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) and online brand-related activities across national contexts. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 815 Generation Z consumers in Chile, Germany, Austria and Greece. Structural equation modeling was used to examine relationships among the three CSR dimensions and brand loyalty, emotional brand attachment, eWOM and online brand-related activities. Multi-group analysis was conducted to assess cross-national differences. Findings Environmental and economic CSR are positively associated with brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, whereas social CSR is negatively associated with brand loyalty and has no significant effect on emotional brand attachment. Brand loyalty positively influences eWOM, while emotional brand attachment positively influences online brand-related activities. Most structural relationships vary significantly across countries, although the relationship between emotional brand attachment and online brand-related activities remains consistent across countries. Originality/value The study advances CSR research by treating CSR as a multidimensional set of signals rather than a homogeneous construct and examining their differentiated implications for consumer–brand relationships. Integrating TBL with an identity-based perspective from SIT, it shows that different CSR dimensions may carry different relevance for Gen Z consumers, and that their effects vary across natio

latest.title: Designing transparency in AI influencer marketing: a consumer–agency architecture
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to develop an understanding of AI influencer transparency and its effects on affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. Design/methodology/approach This paper presents a conceptual synthesis of influencer marketing, consumer psychology and human–algorithm interaction research. Findings This paper introduces the Consumer–Agency Architecture (CAA) framework, distinguishing between information, control and provenance transparency. CAA posits that effects of transparency on consumer outcomes are driven by reductions in reactance, whether affective or cognitive. Information transparency primarily mitigates affective reactance; control transparency reduces cognitive reactance; and provenance transparency can attenuate both. Lower reactance, in turn, can support the formation of affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. The framework further identifies boundary conditions that either strengthen or weaken the relationship between transparency and reactance. Research limitations/implications This paper proposes a conceptual framework that remains to be empirically tested. It also posits that transparency effects in AI influencer marketing are primarily driven by reactance, not gains in perceived authenticity. The developed model also assumes that transparency forms have distinct rather than additive or even nonlinear effects on cognitive and affective reactance. Such assumptions could be tested in future work. Practical implications Brands and platforms should treat transparency as a portfolio of design levers rather than a single disclosure: match the specific type of transparency to the focal objective, anticipate trade-offs and avoid one-size-fits-all transparency that can erode trust. Socia

latest.title: Digital nostalgia and purchase intention among young consumers: roles of attachment, authenticity and brand trust
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to understand how nostalgia proneness and social media engagement influence consumers’ emotional attachment, perceived authenticity, brand trust and purchase intention in digitally mediated, hyper-connected environments. Based on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework, nostalgia proneness and social media engagement are treated as stimulus factors; emotional attachment and perceived authenticity as organism factors; and brand trust and purchase intention as response factors. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted using survey data collected from 501 consumers across multiple sectors in India. Structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed conceptual framework and examine the direct and mediating relationships among the constructs. Findings Results show that nostalgia proneness positively impacts consumers’ emotional attachment and perceived authenticity. Social media engagement positively affects emotional attachment. Emotional attachment and perceived authenticity significantly predict brand trust, which leads to higher purchase intention among consumers. In addition, emotional attachment fully mediates the impact of nostalgia proneness on consumers’ brand trust. The study contributes to emerging digital nostalgia literature by explaining how algorithmically mediated nostalgic experiences influence young consumers’ emotional and behavioral responses, Gen Z and Millennials in particular. Research limitations/implications First, the study used a cross-sectional research design. A causal relationship among the study’s variables cannot be concluded because of its cross-sectional nature. Researchers can use longitudinal studies in the future to understand nostalgic exper

latest.title: Digital entrepreneurship challenge: the effect of website/app hopping on information usefulness
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine website/app hopping as a digital entrepreneurship challenge that shapes consumers' perceptions of information usefulness. Specifically, the study investigates how Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers' digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products relate to website/app hopping and how website/app hopping is associated with information usefulness. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a two-study mixed-method design. Study 1 draws on semi-structured interviews with 12 small business entrepreneurs to identify key themes related to Gen Z consumers' website/app hopping. Study 2 tests the resulting model using survey data from 314 US Gen Z consumers aged 18–24, analyzed through exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and multi-group moderation analysis. Findings The results show that pragmatism and preference for curated products positively predict website/app hopping, while digital savviness might serve as an enabling condition rather than a direct motivator. Website/app hopping is positively related to information usefulness. Multi-group analysis shows that for low-frequency shoppers, digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products all predict website/app hopping. For high-frequency shoppers, pragmatism is the only significant predictor. These findings suggest that digital savviness may be an enabling condition, while pragmatism is the primary motivational driver. Originality/value This study contributes to digital entrepreneurship by reframing website/app hopping as an entrepreneurial information-management challenge rather than merely a consumer search behavior. It shows how Gen Z consumers verify information across fragmented digital platf

latest.title: Between emotion and ethics: a review of advertising appeals, communication and socially responsible consumption (SRC)
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to provide a literature review of the role of advertising appeal and communication on socially responsible consumption (SRC). It synthesizes 75 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus and/or SSCI from the period of 1990–2025. Design/methodology/approach This review adopted a multi-source, iterative search process, incorporating searches via databases, keyword/journal searching, Google Scholar and backward citation searches. Conducted on August 15, 2025, the search provided partial coverage of 2025 publications. Three-stage screening and author-led quality appraisal were applied. The selected articles were analyzed by publication year, geographical context, methodology, respondent characteristics, theoretical framework and advertising appeal themes. Findings The review reveals a transition from traditional rational-emotional appeals toward integrated sustainable, digital, influencer and identity-based communication. Green and corporate social responsibility appeals emerged after 2010, whereas digital and influencer-based persuasion has been gaining prominence since 2015. Emotional and social appeals tend to produce more persuasive results compared with rational appeals, depending on such factors as credibility, authenticity, culture, generations, consumer identity and communication context. Practical implications The results will assist marketing experts, policymakers and communication strategists in creating context-based, credible, authentic and emotional campaigns aimed at promoting socially responsible behavior. Originality/value This review provides an analysis of fragmented literature on advertising appeals by applying the SRC approach, which highlights the idea that no single appeal is universally effective. Instead, the outcomes depend on

latest.title: Co-designing with Generative AI: consumer participation behaviour and product authenticity
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping consumer–brand interactions, with fashion brands increasingly adopting Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) co-design tools that enable direct consumer participation in product design. This research examines how consumers evaluate the authenticity of the GenAI co-designed products, and how evaluation influences consumers’ future participation with fashion brands. This study further investigates whether consumer self-efficacy and perceived expertise toward the tools serve as key antecedents of the authenticity perceptions. By focusing on an emerging AI-enabled service (GenAI) context, this study expands consumer participation and value co-creation research by offering new insight into the drivers and consequences of the perceived authenticity of the fashion products co-created by GenAI and consumers.

latest.title: A consumer neuroscience approach to examining how augmented reality and QR codes support product and brand sustainability communication in retail settings
latest.abstract: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measures to investigate how these technologies influence consumers’ sustainability perceptions, emotional engagement, and cognitive workload. Participants took part in a simulated shopping experience, where they were exposed to one of three experimental conditions: traditional packaging, smartphone-mediated QR code scanning, and smartphone-mediated Augmented Reality exploration of coffee packaging. Cognitive workload (measured via electroencephalography) and emotional engagement (measured via skin conductance and heart rate) were recorded alongside self-report measures of green company orientation (GCO), green product informativeness (GPI), and brand familiarity. Findings indicate that while both AR and QR codes evoke more positive emotions and lead to higher perceptions of GCO and GPI, AR usage is also associated with higher cognitive workload. Additionally, brand familiarity enhanced self-report scores but not neurophysiological ones, without interacting with the interaction modality. This research provides a multi-level (implicit neurophysiological and explicit self-reported) perspective on the impact of digital packaging formats on sustainability communication. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on how interactive technologies can support effective communication, implicit emotions, and consumer engagement with sustainability in retail environments.

latest.title: Canine Companions in the Digital Age: Exploring Pet-Centric Social Media through the Lens of the Extended Self Theory
latest.abstract: This study investigates how Dutch dog owners use non-commercial Instagram profiles for their dogs and how managing these profiles relates to identity construction and self-perception. Guided by Belk’s Extended Self Theory, the study employed a cross-sectional qualitative design and semi-structured interviews with 10 Dutch women who actively managed Instagram accounts for their dogs without seeking monetization. Narrative analysis focused on structure, style, identity, context, and theme, followed by thematic analysis. Five themes emerged: memory preservation; the human-pet bond; social interaction and community; expression and identity; and consumer behavior and pet products. Participants described Instagram as a digital archive for shared memories, a medium for presenting dogs as family members, a site for developing relationships and support networks, and a space for expressing personality, values, humor, and expertise. The accounts also exposed participants to pet products and peer recommendations, influencing consumer knowledge and behavior. Taken together, the findings indicate that pet Instagram profiles operate as digital extensions of owners’ selves, linking personal identity with the represented identity of the dog and with the social networks surrounding the account. The study extends discussion of the Extended Self Theory into everyday, non-commercial pet-centered social media use.

latest.title: Fan or Foe: How Human Versus Virtual Influencers and Review Type Drive Consumer Brand Hate
latest.abstract: This research explores consumer brand hate reactions to influencer-generated reviews, focusing on differences between human influencers (HIs) and virtual influencers (VIs) and review types (unfair negative, fair negative, positive/control). Using a 2 × 3 between-subjects design, two experiments were conducted: Study 1 in a low-involvement context (café), and Study 2 in a high-involvement context (airline). Across both studies, HIs elicited stronger soft (non-purchase intention, brand switching) and hard (brand boycott, negative word-of-mouth) brand hate intentions than VIs, particularly following unfair negative reviews. Psychological contract breach emerges as the key mechanism linking influencer reviews to brand hate perceptions and intentions. This research introduces a theoretical framework to elucidate psychological factors contributing to brand hate reactions. The findings can help brands and advertisers adjust influencer strategies, including those involving generative artificial intelligence-enabled VIs, to meet consumer expectations, strengthen connections, and prevent brand rejection. The findings help brands manage influencer, including artificial intelligence-enabled VI, communications to mitigate brand hate.

latest.title: Beyond likes and shares: how social media marketing communications build brand equity and drive electronic word-of-mouth in emerging E-commerce markets
latest.abstract: Social media is a primary setting in which consumers form brand judgements and recommend products to others. Yet most studies either examine a single social media communication source or combine firm advertising, peer conversation, consumer reviews and influencer endorsements into one composite construct, so the relative associations of these sources with brand equity are rarely compared within one model. It is also unclear whether perceived performance risk weakens or strengthens the translation of brand equity into electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) intention. Using stimulus–organism–response (SOR) theory as an organising framework, this study models four communication sources social media advertising, social media word of mouth, user-generated content and influencer-generated content as stimuli (S), customer-based brand equity (CBBE) as the organism (O) and eWOM intention as the response (R), with performance risk as a moderator of the CBBE → eWOM path. Survey data from 384 e-commerce consumers in Pakistan were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. All four sources were positively associated with CBBE, with user-generated content showing the largest association (β = 0.432), followed by social media advertising (β = 0.183), influencer-generated content (β = 0.178) and social media word of mouth (β = 0.155). CBBE was strongly associated with eWOM intention (β = 0.695), and, contrary to a simple risk-aversion expectation, performance risk strengthened this association (β = 0.157, p < .001). CBBE transmitted significant indirect effects from each source to eWOM intention; when direct paths were added, the associations of social media advertising, social media word of mouth and user-generated content with eWOM intention were fully transmitted th

latest.title: ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN BRAND EQUITY DIMENSIONS AND TOURISTS’ REVISIT INTENTION AT SANGIRAN WORLD HERITAGE SITE
latest.venue: JELAJAH Journal of Tourism and Hospitality
latest.abstract: Revisit intention is an important indicator of tourism destination sustainability, particularly for heritage destinations that aim to encourage visitors to return. This study examines the influence of brand awareness, brand image, brand loyalty, and brand trust on tourists’ revisit intention at Sangiran, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Sragen, Central Java, Indonesia. This research employs a quantitative associative approach using a cross-sectional survey design. Data were collected from 217 tourists who had visited Sangiran, recruited through accidental (convenience) sampling, and were analysed using multiple linear regression. The model as a whole was significant (F(4, 212) = 43.98, p < 0.001; R² = 0.454; adjusted R² = 0.443), meaning that at least one predictor is related to revisit intention. Partially, brand image (B = 0.402; β = 0.406; p < 0.001) and brand loyalty (B = 0.453; β = 0.334; p < 0.001) were positive and significant predictors, whereas brand awareness (β = −0.020; p = 0.767) and brand trust (β = 0.049; p = 0.461) were not. Brand image was the strongest predictor, although its difference from brand loyalty was not statistically distinguishable. Among the examined variables, brand image emerges as the strongest predictor of tourists’ intention to revisit Sangiran. These findings suggest that visitors’ perceptions of a destination and their attachment to its brand play a more substantial role in encouraging repeat visits than mere recognition or trust. This study highlights the importance of strengthening destination image through distinctive tourism experiences, educational attractions, and consistent destination branding. Furthermore, developing visitor loyalty through meaningful engagement and continuous improvements in destination experiences may contr

latest.title: Word-of-Mouth Dissemination of User-Generated Content and Brand Interaction Strategies in Online Marketing
latest.abstract: Online marketing has gradually shifted from enterprise-dominated information dissemination to content communication involving both businesses and consumers. User-generated content (UGC), as an important means through which consumers express product experiences, share consumption opinions, and participate in brand communication, has become a major source of online word-of-mouth. Consumers transform their personal consumption experiences into publicly accessible information through product reviews, usage experiences, videos, images, and comments, thereby influencing other consumers' brand perceptions and purchasing decisions. Meanwhile, UGC provides businesses with new opportunities to understand consumer needs, improve products and services, and establish brand relationships. However, several problems remain in current online marketing practices, including insufficient content authenticity, repetitive content, superficial brand interactions, and delayed responses to negative reviews. Businesses need to improve their marketing strategies in terms of content authenticity, user participation mechanisms, interactive feedback, and long-term brand relationship management. By doing so, they can transform UGC into a sustainable resource for brand communication and promote the transition from one-way promotion to two-way communication.

latest.title: Marketing d'influence et comportement omnicanal du consommateur : rôle médiateur de la confiance envers les enseignes de grande distribution au Maroc
latest.venue: International Journal of Research in Economics and Finance
latest.abstract: Cette étude analyse la manière dont le marketing d’influence et l’engagement communautaire sur les réseaux sociaux contribuent au comportement omnicanal des consommateurs marocains, en examinant le rôle médiateur de la confiance envers les enseignes de grande distribution. Dans une démarche hypothético-déductive, le modèle intègre le marketing d’influence comme construit composite d’ordre supérieur, composé de cinq dimensions (crédibilité, expertise, attractivité, congruence influenceur–enseigne et interactivité), ainsi que l’engagement communautaire, la confiance envers l’enseigne et le comportement omnicanal. Sept hypothèses sont évaluées auprès de 280 consommateurs marocains qui suivent des influenceurs et fréquentent des enseignes de grande distribution. Les données sont analysées avec SPSS 26, SmartPLS 4.0 (PLS-SEM) et Stata 17, cette dernière analyse servant de test de robustesse par régression logistique. Cinq hypothèses sont soutenues. L’effet direct du marketing d’influence sur le comportement omnicanal (H4) et l’effet modérateur de la fréquence d’exposition sur la relation entre marketing d’influence et confiance (H7) ne sont pas statistiquement significatifs. La régression logistique suggère toutefois un effet direct résiduel et modeste du marketing d’influence sur la décision d’adopter un parcours omnicanal. Le modèle explique 56,4 % de la variance de la confiance et 48,6 % de celle du comportement omnicanal. Ces résultats soulignent le rôle de la confiance dans la conversion des interactions avec les influenceurs en comportements entre canaux et éclairent les choix de collaboration des enseignes de grande distribution.

latest.title: Cognitive and emotional mechanisms influencing consumer brand loyalty through digital interpersonal interaction
latest.venue: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
latest.abstract: The digital interaction between consumers and brands is becoming increasingly like interpersonal interaction as consumers receive personalized responses, an empathic tone of voice, feedback, and social presence via social media platforms, chatbot interactions, and other message exchange platforms. The current research examines a relational process model that investigates the effect of perceived quality of digital interpersonal interaction on the level of consumer brand loyalty via brand credibility and emotional attachment. Social presence theory, signaling theory, attachment theory, and consumer-brand relationship theories were utilized to develop this model, where credibility is seen as a cognitive evaluation, and attachment is defined as emotional connection. Cross-sectional survey methodology was employed, where adults who have interacted with a brand via any digital touchpoint in the past three months were approached (N = 438). The empirical results reveal that there is a positive correlation between interaction quality and credibility (β = .54, p < .001), and attachment (β = .49, p < .001), both serve as a predictor of loyalty (β = .28, p < .001) and (β = .44, p < .001), respectively, but interaction quality still maintains a positive relationship with loyalty (β = .14, p = .002), 95% CI ([.06, .22])) after taking into consideration both mechanisms. Such an outcome is achieved despite demographic and relationship variables controlled in the research, which proves the validity of the proposed mechanism. The emotional indirect effect (β = .22), 95% CI ([.16, .29]) is more prominent than the cognitive effect (β = .15), 95% CI ([.10, .21]), meaning that the positive and personally concerned interaction transmits a greater part of the loyalty effect than credibility do

latest.title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. Structural equation modeling was used to test the dual-mediation model involving perceived value and environmental concern. Findings Brand image positively influences both perceived value and environmental concern. Perceived value enhances purchase intention, while environmental concern suppresses it. Both variables significantly mediate the brand–purchase relationship in opposing directions, with an overall positive indirect effect, suggesting that brand resilience endures despite ecological concerns. Originality/value This study contributes by modeling competing psychological mediators in seafood consumption under environmental threat, an area that has received limited attention in existing literature. It reveals consumer ambivalence during ecological crises: while strong brands retain appeal, environmental risk awareness weakens purchasing confidence. The findings offer actionable insights for seafood marketers on sustaining brand resilience through value communication and transparent sustainability practices.

latest.title: Religiosity and consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z: does gender make a difference?
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how religiosity is associated with consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z in a highly religious emerging market. It proposes the spiritual cognitive consumption theory (SCCT), a dual pathway framework, and provides preliminary empirical support for its overall predictive validity. However, these two pathways were not directly measured; future experimental research is needed to isolate each mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 400 Nigerian respondents were analysed using structural equation modelling. Gender significantly moderates this relationship: women tend to show a stronger association between religiosity and relational aspects (e.g. brand trust, emotional congruity), whereas men focus more on instrumental outcomes (e.g. product functionality, religious symbolism). Findings The SCCT framework provides a nuanced understanding of the tension between spiritual devotion and market-based consumption. The findings offer marketers gender-sensitive, faith-conscious strategies and position SCCT as a robust theoretical tool for understanding spirituality, cognition and consumption in evolving digital economies. Social implications The study contributes to sustainable development goal (SDG) 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by providing insights into inclusive, faith-sensitive marketing practices in the Global South. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in the development of the SCCT framework, which integrates spirituality, cognition and consumption into a dual pathway model. This offers a novel theoretical lens for understanding consumer behaviour in religious emerging markets.

latest.title: The Impact of Internal Branding on Brand Attitudes of Customers in the IT Industry: An empirical Study
authors: Malan begum Zardi Dr Charu Bisaria
latest.abstract: Internal branding has emerged as a critical strategic tool in the IT industry, where customer loyalty and brand differentiation are increasingly shaped by employees’ alignment with organizational values. This empirical study investigates the impact of internal branding on brand attitudes of customers, with a focus on demographic dimensions such as age, educational qualification, and job designation. Using a structured questionnaire, data were collected from 200 respondents representing various roles and educational backgrounds in the IT sector. The study employed chi-square analysis to test the association between demographic variables and perceptions of the impact of internal branding. However, the results of chi-square tests indicate no statistically significant relationship between demographic factors and perceptions of internal branding effectiveness, suggesting that the influence of internal branding is relatively consistent across diverse groups. The study contributes to the literature by demonstrating that internal branding strategies can be uniformly applied in the IT industry without significant variation in effectiveness across different demographic profiles. This highlights the universal importance of internal branding practices in fostering positive brand attitudes among customers.

latest.title: Digital marketing strategies and their relationship with customer loyalty in poultry companies in Northern Peru
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe accelerated adoption of digital communication channels has transformed customer relationship management in the poultry sector, particularly in emerging economies where companies face increasing competitive pressure and limited differentiation. In Peru’s poultry industry, many firms have incorporated digital tools into their commercial activities; however, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty remains limited. This study aims to analyze the relationship between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty in poultry companies located in the Northern Highlands of Peru. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional, and correlational research design was adopted. Data were collected through structured surveys administered to 150 customers who made recurring purchases via digital channels between January and March 2025. Given the non-normal distribution of the data, Spearman’s rho coefficient was used for statistical analysis. The results revealed a strong and statistically significant positive association between digital marketing strategies and customer loyalty (ρ = 0.898; p < 0.001). High correlations were also identified between customer loyalty and specific dimensions of digital marketing, including tangible digital aspects (ρ = 0.854), digital promotions (ρ = 0.826), and digital responsiveness (ρ = 0.831). A complementary multiple regression analysis showed that the three dimensions remained significantly associated with customer loyalty when considered simultaneously, explaining 82.2% of its variance (R2 = 0.822). In conclusion, the findings indicate that digital communication quality, promotional strategies, and rapid responsiveness may contribu

latest.title: Brand Experience Strategy in Building Wardah's Brand Awareness Through Skinverse Campaign
latest.abstract: Brands with already high levels of brand awareness face challenges that differ from those of emerging brands, particularly in maintaining relevance and memorability amid increasingly intense competition. This study examines Wardah's brand experience strategy through the Skinverse campaign, which was conducted in 2024, 2025, and 2026, and its potential contribution to brand awareness. The study employs a qualitative approach with a case study design based on document analysis. Data were obtained from company press releases, 17 articles published by national online media outlets, and Top Brand Index data from 2022 to 2026. These sources were analyzed through deductive coding based on Schmitt's five Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs). The findings reveal that Skinverse evolved from a science-based educational exhibition in 2024 to an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered skincare clinic in 2025, followed by a skin longevity clinic integrating skin health with lifestyle factors in 2026. Throughout this evolution, the experiential emphasis shifted from the Think module toward the Act module. The document analysis identified four potential mechanisms for strengthening brand awareness: the consistent use of the Skinverse campaign name as a distinctive brand asset; MURI (Indonesian World Records Museum) records and collaborations with experts as drivers of media coverage; personalized artifacts, such as the Skin ID Blueprint, as memory cues; and the expansion of brand associations into skin science and healthy lifestyles. However, the study also found that the campaign's contributions to brand awareness could not be directly substantiated by the Top Brand Index data for the facial moisturizer category.

latest.title: Theoretical Analysis of the Formation Path of Social Identity and Virtual Community Belonging on Brand Loyalty
latest.venue: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: With the rise of internet technology and social media, virtual communities have become important platforms for communication between brands and consumers, playing an increasingly significant role in shaping brand loyalty. Based on social identity theory and social belonging theory, this paper summarizes consumer psychological cognition and behavioral responses within virtual communities, analyzing how social identity and community belonging influence the formation of brand loyalty. First, it outlines the relationships among social identity, virtual community belonging, and brand loyalty by defining these concepts. Then, drawing on relevant literature and theoretical reasoning, it proposes a theoretical model—"social identity → community belonging → brand loyalty"—to explain how consumers gradually develop brand loyalty through identity recognition, group interaction, and emotional connection within virtual communities. Next, by examining the classification, comparison, and psychologization of social identity, the paper analyzes how individuals identify with brand communities through self-categorization and group affiliation, and further explores how community belonging acts as a mediator in influencing consumer trust, emotional attachment, and willingness to continue participation. The study argues that social identity strengthens consumers' sense of group identity, making them more receptive to the values and culture of brand communities, while virtual community belonging enhances the psychological contract between consumers and brands through emotional bonds and interactive experiences—both contributing positively to the development of brand loyalty. Additionally, the paper discusses the impact of factors such as community atmosphere, interaction frequency, and inform

latest.title: A Theoretical Study on the Conceptual Integration of Plasticity and Resilience in Lifespan Developmental Psychology
latest.venue: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Over decades, lifespan developmental psychology has gradually developed a research paradigm centered on the entire life course. Within this framework, "plasticity" and "resilience" have emerged as two key concepts, each reflecting human development from different perspectives—plasticity emphasizing changeability and adaptability, while resilience highlighting stability and stress resistance. However, for a long time, these two constructs have often been studied separately in both theoretical construction and empirical research: plasticity primarily focuses on the potential and extent of changes in cognition, emotion, and behavior due to internal or external influences, underscoring openness and malleability in development; resilience, by contrast, examines individuals' capacity to maintain or restore optimal functioning after facing adversity, setbacks, or stress, emphasizing developmental stability and coping strength. This separation has limited the explanatory power of existing theories, making it difficult to fully account for the coexistence of change and continuity, vulnerability and strength throughout development. This article, grounded in the holistic perspective of lifespan developmental psychology, reviews the origins, meanings, and applications of plasticity and resilience in lifespan research, and compares their similarities and differences in theoretical assumptions, research methods, and measurement tools. It argues for the possibility and necessity of integrating these two concepts. The paper contends that plasticity serves as a prerequisite for resilience—what people demonstrate as resilience in times of hardship is essentially a manifestation of plasticity under specific conditions. Conversely, the development of resilience also shapes future developme

latest.title: The Role of Branding in Enhancing the Perceived Marketing Value of Sports Clubs: An Analytical Field Study of Selected Clubs in Wasit Province, Iraq
latest.abstract: Sports clubs increasingly depend on the strength of their brands to retain supporters and attract commercial partners, yet strong fan attachment does not automatically translate into sponsorship, merchandising or revenue. This study examined the relationship between five dimensions of branding (identity, awareness, image, perceived quality and loyalty) and five dimensions of perceived marketing value (fan, sponsorship, media/digital, financial and merchandising value) among stakeholders of three sports clubs in Wasit Province, Iraq. A descriptive–analytical cross-sectional survey was conducted with 264 respondents (200 supporters, 34 players and 30 coaches and administrators) selected by stratified random sampling. Data were collected with a 42-item five-point Likert questionnaire (Cronbach’s α = 0.94) and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, one-way ANOVA with Tukey–Kramer post hoc tests and independent-samples t tests. Overall branding was rated high (M = 3.59, SD = 0.62), whereas perceived marketing value was moderate (M = 3.09, SD = 0.66). Loyalty was the strongest branding dimension (M = 3.94) and perceived quality the weakest (M = 3.18); among the value dimensions, fan value scored highest (M = 3.71) and merchandising lowest (M = 2.68). Branding correlated strongly with perceived marketing value (r = 0.781, p < .001), and the five dimensions together explained 65.9% of its variance (F(5, 258) = 99.72, p < .001). Loyalty (β = 0.298) and perceived quality (β = 0.241) were the strongest unique predictors. The results reveal a gap between stakeholder attachment and the clubs’ commercial capacity. Improving service quality and building professional sponsorship and merchandising systems may help clubs convert brand stre

latest.title: Are Prediction Platform Bettors Distinct from Sportsbook Bettors? Evidence from Skill Perceptions and Positive Play Attitudes
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of sports betting in the United States has been accompanied by the emergence of prediction market platforms offering sports event contracts, which closely resemble traditional wagering while differing in how they are framed and regulated. This study examines whether individuals who buy and sell sports event contracts differ from sportsbook bettors in their perceptions of skill versus luck and their positive play attitudes. Data were collected from two separate samples of U.S. participants recruited through Prolific, including sportsbook bettors (n = 523) and prediction market users (n = 503). A multivariate analysis of covariance (MANCOVA) was conducted to assess group differences across perceived skill, perceived luck, and four dimensions of Positive Play: gambling literacy, honesty and control, personal responsibility, and pre-commitment. Results indicate that prediction market users report significantly higher perceived skill and lower perceived luck compared to sportsbook bettors. Additionally, prediction market users exhibit lower levels of gambling literacy, honesty and control, and personal responsibility. These findings suggest a misalignment between perceived control and responsible engagement among prediction market users. The study contributes to emerging research on sports wagering by highlighting the importance of understanding consumer behavior across differing wagering platforms and offers implications for consumer protection in the evolving sports wagering space.

latest.title: Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience in Generation Z Loyalty: Customer Engagement as a Mediator
latest.abstract: Objectives: This study examines the effects of Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience on Customer Loyalty among Generation Z consumers of Erigo, with Customer Engagement as a mediating variable.Methodology: This study employed a quantitative explanatory research design using a cross-sectional survey of 250 respondents aged 17–29 who had purchased Erigo products through multiple channels. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0.Finding: The results show that Omnichannel Integration has a positive and significant effect on Customer Engagement (β = 0.335; p < 0.001) and Customer Loyalty (β = 0.159; p = 0.006). Similarly, Seamless Experience positively and significantly affects Customer Engagement (β = 0.317; p < 0.001) and Customer Loyalty (β = 0.197; p < 0.001). Furthermore, Customer Engagement has a positive and significant effect on Customer Loyalty (β = 0.400; p < 0.001). The results also demonstrate that Customer Engagement plays a mediating role in the relationship between Omnichannel Integration, Seamless Experience, and Customer Loyalty.Conclusion: This study concludes that Omnichannel Integration and Seamless Experience contribute to enhancing Customer Loyalty, both directly and indirectly through Customer Engagement. Customer Engagement serves as an important mediating mechanism that transforms integrated and seamless omnichannel experiences into stronger customer loyalty. These findings support the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework in the context of Generation Z consumers of Erigo.

latest.title: DIGITAL ENTREPRENEURIAL TRANSFORMATION IN THE PESANTREN ECOSYSTEM: EVIDENCE FROM PESANTREN AL AMIN KEDIRI, INDONESIA
latest.abstract: Pesantren, as traditional Islamic educational institutions, increasingly adopt digital technologies to strengthen economic self-reliance through entrepreneurship. This study aimed to analyze digital marketing strategies implemented by santri at Pesantren Al Amin Kediri and their contributions to business development. This research employed a descriptive qualitative case study approach. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, documentation, and digital content analysis of Instagram, WhatsApp Business, and TikTok. The analysis integrated the Digital Marketing Framework and Resource-Based View (RBV) to examine digital capabilities and internal resources as sources of competitive advantage. The findings indicate that santri contribute to digital transformation through content creation, social media engagement, digital branding, and online customer communication. These practices have expanded the market reach of Al Amin Bordir dan Konveksi, enhanced brand visibility, and strengthened customer relationships. Spiritual values, entrepreneurial learning, and alumni networks further reinforce customer trust and business sustainability. The study contributes theoretically by extending the application of RBV to pesantren-based digital entrepreneurship, demonstrating how spiritual values, social capital, and trust-based relationships complement technological capabilities in creating competitive advantage. Practically, the study contributes an integrated approach to digital entrepreneurship that emphasizes santri empowerment, digital marketing skills, and alumni engagement while preserving religious and cultural identities. This study concludes that digital marketing functions not merely as a promotional instrument but also as a mechanism for entre

latest.title: THE CORRELATION BETWEEN PAYLATER USAGE AND DISCOUNT PROMOTIONS WITH THE CONSUMERIST BEHAVIOR OF COLLEGE STUDENTS
latest.abstract: ABSTRACTThe problem from this research indicate that the majority of college students in the Economics Education Program at STKIP PGRI Lumajang are experiencing a shift in their consumption patterns toward consumerism. This study aims to examine the relationship between the use of PayLater services and discount promotions with students’ consumerism behavior. The research method used in this study by quantitative descriptive method with correlation analysis. Data were collected by questionnaires and analyzed using Pearson’s correlation, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination. The research findings indicate that the use of paylater services has a strong positive correlation with the consumerist behavior of students in the Economics Education program. Another finding shows that discount promotions have a strong positive relationship with the consumerism behavior of students in the Economics Education program. Finally conclude this study, the simultaneous use of paylater services and discount promotions has a strong positive correlation with the consumerism behavior of students in the Economics Education program. Contributions to the Economics Education Program are expected to improve financial literacy through seminars, training sessions, or educational programs on the use of financial services. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji hubungan antara penggunaan layanan paylater dan promosi diskon dengan perilaku konsumerisme mahasiswa. Metode penelitian yang digunakan dalam

latest.title: The Influence of Sales Promotion Content, Content Attractiveness, and User-Friendliness on Financial Decision Making through Imitation Intention
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the influence of sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness on financial decision making through imitation intention among social media users in Indonesia, particularly in the context of influencer marketing for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the food and beverage sector. Research Method: This study uses a quantitative explanatory design with a cross-sectional approach. Data are collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and purposive sampling. Data analysis employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. Results and Discussion: The study proposes that sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness influence imitation intention and financial decision making. Imitation intention is also expected to influence financial decision making and mediate the relationships between promotional content characteristics and financial decisions. These relationships will be evaluated empirically. Implications: The findings are expected to help MSMEs and influencers develop promotional strategies that encourage informed financial decisions among social media users. Future research may examine other factors affecting consumer financial behavior. Originality: This study integrates three influencer promotional content characteristics with imitation intention to explain financial decision making in the Indonesian MSME food and beverage sector.

latest.title: The Psychological Mechanisms of Scarcity Marketing on Gen Z Impulse Buying Behavior in Malaysia: A Conceptual Framework
latest.abstract: Scarcity marketing has become a dominant persuasive strategy in digital retail, yet its psychological impact on Generation Z consumers in Malaysia remains underexplored. This concept paper proposes a conceptual framework examining the psychological mechanisms through which scarcity marketing influences impulse buying behavior among Malaysian Gen Z consumers. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and integrating Commodity Theory and Social Comparison Theory, the framework posits that three scarcity marketing stimuli—time-limited, quantity-limited, and social proof scarcity—activate four psychological mediators: fear of missing out (FOMO), competitive arousal, perceived urgency, and social comparison, which subsequently drive impulse buying behavior. The framework further proposes that self-control, digital literacy, financial literacy, and brand trust moderate these relationships. Drawing upon a systematic review of literature from 2017 to 2026, this paper synthesizes empirical evidence demonstrating that FOMO exerts the strongest mediating influence on impulse buying, while self-control consistently weakens the relationship between psychological mediators and behavioral outcomes. The proposed framework contributes to consumer behavior theory by clarifying the mediating pathways and boundary conditions of scarcity marketing effects and offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers and consumer educators in developing responsible marketing practices and targeted digital literacy interventions. Empirical validation through quantitative survey methods targeting 400 Malaysian Gen Z consumers aged 18–27 is proposed to test the hypothesized relationships using Structural Equation Modelling.

latest.title: Institutional legitimacy, digital marketing, and holistic customer experiences in agamid lizard-based gastronomy
latest.abstract: This paper explores how institutional legitimacy facilitates holistic value co-creation in unconventional food service ecosystems, explaining this through the mediating roles of quality control and trust in health authorities. Specifically, this paper examines how the institutional and operational legitimacy mechanisms supporting agamid lizard menu items contribute to comprehensive service experiences from customer perspectives. Data were obtained from 612 customers who had previously experienced restaurant ecosystems in hot deserts in Nigeria. Results showed that customer solidarity positively affects customer perceptions of quality control and trust in health authorities, as well as their service experiences. Findings also indicated that digital marketing practices strengthened the relationship between quality control and holistic experiences, enhancing the experiential value of operational legitimacy signals. This paper combines institutional theory and experiential marketing theory to advance research on the relationship between legitimacy mechanisms and customer experiences in unconventional gastronomic ecosystems and provide insights into customer value co-creation in high-risk gastronomic services.

latest.title: Gamification in Digital Marketing: Enhancing Engagement and Loyalty
latest.abstract: In the contemporary digital marketplace, consumer attention has become increasingly fragmented due to information overload and constant exposure to competing stimuli. Traditional marketing strategies often fail to sustain meaningful engagement, necessitating innovative approaches that integrate motivational design with experiential value. This paper proposes the Gamified Experiential Marketing Framework (GEMF), a novel conceptual model that unites gamification mechanics with experiential marketing principles to address declining consumer attention and foster sustainable brand loyalty. Drawing upon Self-Determination Theory, Flow Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model, GEMF explains how gamification elements such as points, badges, leaderboards, and narratives activate psychological mediators of motivation, experiential value, and emotional engagement. These mediators, moderated by contextual factors including platform characteristics, cultural context, and demographics, lead to enhanced consumer engagement, loyalty, and immersive brand experiences. The paper contributes theoretically by bridging gamification and experiential marketing, offering a holistic framework that positions gamification as a motivational engine within digital marketing.
